jobs.title: IT Operations & Security Lead (Remote - US CT/ET)
jobs.description:
IT Operations & Security Lead
 
Location: Remote (CT/ET Timezone). Collaborating with teams on the West Coast and in Europe, alongside building out a new hub in Chicago.
Type: Full-time
Salary: Location dependent. As a guide, our current range across all levels is up to $120k. We are open to negotiation as we recognise there are different situations, but this is our general guardrail.
🌍 Our vision
Every child deserves a better start toward the best possible future. The right educator in the right classroom at the right time can change a child’s chances and, at scale, a nation’s trajectory. Yet too much of our education system’s time, money, and talent are lost to inefficiency.
At Zen Educate, we’re changing that through technology: helping schools save millions in tight times, helping educators find work that rewards their skills and fits their lives, and building a better-educated society that invests its best in every child.
What I’m looking for
👋 Hi, I’m Martin, Chief Technology Officer at Zen Educate, and I’m looking for someone to own Zen’s internal IT systems and security as we grow. You’ll report directly to me as part of our new Business Systems team, and you’ll be the first dedicated hire to replace what has so far been spread across several roles.
I’ll lean on you to execute well and to show the way on modern IT and security practice, including automation, governance and AI adoption. Your north star is a clear, proportionate, defensible and scalable IT and security posture, for the company Zen is today and the one it’s growing into.
That means fixing the problem in front of you, while making sure nobody has to fix it manually again tomorrow.
So this probably isn’t the role for you if you solely enjoy clearing ticket queues or becoming very good at provisioning accounts by hand.
It might be if your instinct is: why are we still doing this manually, and who do I need to work with to fix it?
My ideal hire:
has seen what great looks like and now wants to build their version of it from scratch;
takes this headspace off my plate, while keeping me informed and involved on the decisions that matter;
communicates confidently at every level of the business to get things done;
treats every pound spent here as a pound not spent elsewhere on our mission: investing confidently where it matters, cutting what doesn’t, and making the return easy to see.
Where we are and where we need to go
Zen now has around 600 people across the UK and US (not counting the educators we place in schools), and our IT and security practices need to grow with us.
Up to now, we’ve kept pace with that growth through good people, manual processes and a few well-kept spreadsheets. It’s worked well. But our growth has steepened recently (yay!), and the cracks and inefficiencies are starting to show.
More people have joined and more software has been bought. We found two company accounts for the same tool, one with a single admin who didn't know they were an admin. Permissions have multiplied and devices are spread across locations. When someone leaves, we work through a long list of accounts to deactivate, with the nagging feeling we’ve missed one.
None of these are particularly unusual on their own, and so far we’ve handled them case by case. But because the responsibility is spread across roles, nobody has the time to build the systems that would make these problems irrelevant, or even turn them into opportunities.
That’s what we want you to solve as we scale. We want an internal environment where:
our confidence in our posture is high, and justified;
people get the tools and access they need, quickly, with clear governance over what “need” means;
we’re secure by default, not because someone remembered;
“why do we have this?” and “is it still good value?” are easy to answer for any tool;
audits get more boring each year because the evidence already exists.
We want people at Zen to finish an IT or security request thinking “wow, that was easy”, and occasionally “I didn’t know we needed that, but I’m glad we have it”.
What the role looks like in practice
This is a new role at Zen, so part of the job is defining what it looks like. These are the problems we already know you’ll be working on.
🔑 Identity and access
We still grant access to several systems by hand when someone joins. You could improve the checklist. We’d rather you built the workflow that makes the checklist disappear.
You’ll own internal identity and access: Google Workspace, SSO, MFA, groups, permissions and "least privilege" as a principle. Access should follow people as they join, move and leave, not depend on someone remembering to remove it.
🧹 SaaS sprawl
We use a lot of software. Some of it is essential. Some probably isn’t. Some have 80 licences and 37 active users.
You’ll build the definitive view of our software and service estate (what we use, who owns it, who has access, what it costs, when it renews) and work with teams and vendors to improve how we buy, renew and retire tools.
🛡️ Security that works
Policies are useful. Policies people understand and follow are far more useful.
You’ll define and maintain our IT and security policies, then turn them into working processes, technical controls and training that sticks: access reviews, vulnerability management, external testing, incident processes and an easy way to report concerns.
📋 Trust, assurance and compliance
Customers increasingly want evidence that we take security seriously. You’ll make that evidence easy to provide: security questionnaires, audit evidence, Cyber Essentials and future certifications, risk management and governance. Certifications should follow real controls, not stand in for them.
Rather than answering every questionnaire from scratch, you’ll build a reusable, increasingly self-service trust process. Where security meets privacy, you’ll work closely with our Legal and Data Protection advisors.
💻 The device fleet
Devices need to be secure, patched, encrypted and accounted for wherever people work, and not all of them are company-owned. You’ll set a proportionate approach to personal devices alongside endpoint management for our own fleet. Our People Team handles ordering and delivery; you’ll make sure every device is set up and provisioned securely, remotely, through to retirement.
When a critical vulnerability lands, we want to know which devices are affected, what needs to happen, and that it actually happened within our 14-day patching window.
🚨 When something goes wrong
Things will go wrong. A vendor has an incident. A device falls out of compliance. Someone finds access that shouldn’t exist.
Your job isn’t to guarantee nothing happens. It’s to make sure we respond well: clear ownership, good communication, recorded decisions, and the underlying issue actually fixed. We already have an established incident process for our product; you’ll extend it to everything else.
What this role doesn’t own
It covers corporate IT and security, not the platform we build as our product.
Product and platform security sits with our Foundations Lead and Engineering. You’ll coordinate with them on company-wide initiatives such as least privilege, and may drive them as overall lead.
The wider employee lifecycle sits with our People Team. You’ll own the systems, access and devices that support it, and help automate it where you can.
Internal data architecture and bespoke data tooling sit with your peer in Business Systems. Different lens, often the same problems: you’ll work together a lot.
Final budget decisions on tools and services sit with me and other senior leaders. You’ll provide the visibility and recommendations to make them well.
What you might like or dislike
Every place makes trade-offs based on what it values and where it is in its journey ⚖️. Here are some that might help you decide whether this is the right role for you. If we end up chatting, feel free to dig into any of them. Some are recent changes in our approach and may still be work in progress when you join.
🛠️ How we work
Build systems, not queues. We see IT as a systems problem, not an administration problem. If something happens repeatedly, challenge whether it still needs a person, whether the answer is scripting, APIs, workflow tools, AI, native platform automation or simply a better process. This is hands-on: you might discuss security posture with leadership in the morning and fix an access workflow in the afternoon. Either way, today’s fix should shrink tomorrow’s workload.
Proven tools for the obvious, experimentation for the rest. Where a mature tool does the job well, use it rather than building our own. Where nothing does, we’d rather you tried something new, AI included, than accept friction simply because that’s how it’s always been done.
Security that enables the business. We want stronger security without theatre or needless friction. That takes judgement: telling a meaningful risk from a theoretical one, and both from one we can reasonably accept. Sometimes the answer is to lock something down, sometimes a better process, sometimes to accept the risk and move on. Whatever it is, you’ll explain clearly what’s happening, why it matters and what happens next.
Be visible and own the outcome. IT and security usually only get noticed when access breaks or someone is told no. We’d like you to change that: a recognisable, approachable go-to person who brings energy to the space, builds confidence in where we stand and follows problems through to the end.
🌱 Growth & progression
Choose your own career path. We care more about impact and learning than rigid competency grids. That gives more flexibility in what progression looks like, but means building an understanding of what we value from guiding principles and shared real-world examples.
Your manager is a partner, not a supervisor. I won’t direct your every move. Expect me to help you think through hard problems, offer perspective and nudge you to grow, not to tell you what to do or check your work. You’ll need to own your progress and speak up when you need unblocking.
Few titles, infinite levels. Across Technology we use Levels, not titles, to show growth in a role. Lead is the role; you grow within it by getting better at it, for example working faster, safer and more independently. Changing roles is possible too, but depends on business needs.
Investment over reward. Level changes are tightly coupled to compensation changes, and are based on sustainably doing great work at your current level. We think it’s fairer to invest in what you do next than to reward you for doing the next level first for free.
💸 Compensation
Market reality. Compensation is based on your competitiveness in your local hiring market (which isn’t just where you live). Nobody has found a great solution to global compensation, so we aim to be clear and equitable in how we do it.
Solid, not flashy. We pay decently, but we won’t beat companies with deeper pockets (yet!).
Think long term. If you need to prioritise immediate financial gain, this probably isn’t the right time to join us. 
🤝 Team culture & collaboration
Remote, but close to the business. This role is remote and serves teams across the UK and US, most of whom aren’t in Technology. Strong communication and async habits are key, and you’ll need to understand how frontline teams actually work, not just how their systems are configured.
Impact and measurable outcomes, alongside shared learning. If your work moves the needle or teaches us something meaningful, that’s a win. If not, we’ll want to understand why.
Balanced, sustainable work. Long hours aren’t a badge of honour; they’re a sign something isn’t working. We value a sustainable pace and healthy teams.
Diversity is good in some ways and lacking in others. You might be the first of something here. That matters, and we’ll support you appropriately if you are.
You’ve probably done this before
Maybe you were the second or third person in an IT, Corporate IT or Security Operations team while a company grew from a few hundred people to something much larger. You’ve seen what breaks, helped fix it, and now want to own the playbook.
We care more about what you’ve actually improved than whether your CV lists every tool we use. We’d expect real hands-on depth in identity and access, endpoint management and automation, and a working grasp of the rest: SaaS governance, vendor and licence management, audits and certification, incident response and data protection.
Beyond that, we’re hiring for principles over product knowledge. You should know more about security than I do, understand why controls work well enough to get to grips with any system yourself, and be business-minded enough to apply it in proportion to where Zen is today, knowing which risks actually matter for us.
How we hire
We want the process to be useful for both sides, not an obstacle course. There are three stages.
1. Recruiter chat. A conversation with our People Team about the environments you’ve worked in and the areas where you think your experience is most relevant to Zen.
2. Role deep dive with me. Your experience actually implementing change. We’re most interested in something you took from manual, messy or poorly defined to scalable so feel free to come with a prepared example to discuss. I'll also want to explore how you think about IT and security from a modern perspective (including what good looks like at Zen’s stage, and how you’d know we’re genuinely there), how you balance the tradeoff between progress and perfection, how you build confidence, and how we'll work together. Expect a conversation where I'll be as interested in the questions you ask as the answers you give.
3. Team session. You’ll present to the people you’d work with most closely, across Foundations, Business Systems, People and Finance. We’ll send you a short scenario in advance: someone joins Zen, moves team and leaves within a year. Walk us through how their access, tools and licences should follow them, and how you’d get us from where we are today to where we need to be.
We don’t expect you to have all the answers. We do expect a point of view (and for you to ask lots of questions of the team to build the picture).
Interested?
If you read this and started thinking about everything you’d automate, improve or rebuild, we should talk. And if turning slightly messy internal systems into something secure, scalable and boringly reliable sounds genuinely satisfying, even better 🚀

Every organization is asking the same question right now: do I have the real-time visibility I need to stay secure and put AI to work safely? Tanium's autonomous, agentic platform - built on nearly two decades of real-time telemetry across 36 million+ endpoints worldwide - is the answer. Proven platform, frontier AI, real stakes -  that's the moment Tanium is in right now.

As our Senior Technical Recruiter, you'll own full-cycle recruiting for some of our most competitive, highest-impact technical roles - backed by a best-in-class, AI-enabled stack (recruiting tools like Noon.AI and BrightHire, plus enterprise AI like Claude for everyday work) built to strip out busywork so you can spend your time on judgment calls, not admin. This role covers a variety of technical requisitions rather than one narrow lane, so it rewards curiosity and learning agility over deep specialization in any single domain. Our environment moves fast and priorities shift often. If that kind of ambiguity energizes you, you'll get broad exposure across teams and real room to build influence quickly.

This position follows the Company’s hybrid schedule which currently requires employees to work in the office at one of the following locations a minimum of three days per week: Durham, NC or Emeryville, CA.

What you’ll do:

Do našeho týmu proto hledáme kolegu nebo kolegyni, který/á bude přímo ve skladu hlídat kvalitu zboží – od chvíle, kdy k nám dorazí, během jeho skladování až po cestu k zákazníkovi.

Pokud máš dobré oko pro detail, jsi pečlivý/á a nebojíš se říct, když něco není v pořádku, tahle práce by Ti mohla sednout. Předchozí zkušenosti z kvality jsou výhodou, ale důležitější je pro nás spolehlivost, zodpovědnost a chuť dělat věci pořádně.



Co Tě u nás čeká

 - Budeš kontrolovat kvalitu zboží při příjmu a hlídat, zda odpovídá našim standardům.

 - Průběžně zkontroluješ produkty také během skladování a oddělíš zboží, které požadovanou kvalitu nesplňuje.

 - Výsledky kontrol budeš jednoduše zaznamenávat, aby bylo vždy dohledatelné, co a kdy se kontrolovalo.

 - Pokud narazíš na problém, předáš ho nadřízenému a pomůžeš s jeho řešením.

 - Budeš se podílet na zavádění nápravných opatření, aby se stejné problémy zbytečně neopakovaly.

 - Čeká Tě práce přímo v provozu skladu, včetně chladírenských prostor.
   
   

Hodíš se k nám, pokud:

 - máš smysl pro detail a přesnost,

 - je na tebe spoleh a umíš dodržovat nastavené postupy,

 - dokážeš jasně komunikovat a upozornit na problém,

 - nevadí Ti směnný provoz,

 - zvládneš práci ve skladovém prostředí včetně chladnějších prostor,

 - poradíš si s mobilem, aplikacemi a jednoduchým zadáváním dat,

 - a umíš fungovat jako součást týmu.
   
   

Co je výhodou, ale ne podmínkou

 - SŠ vzdělání v oblasti potravinářství, zemědělství nebo příbuzném oboru.

 - Zkušenost ze skladu, maloobchodu, potravinářské výroby nebo kontroly kvality.

 - Základní znalost angličtiny.
   
   

Co Ti nabízíme:

 - Rohlík Xtra účet zdarma – nakupování s 10% cashbackem v podobě kreditů na další nákupy.

 - Možnost placeného volna – čas na pořádný odpočinek a regeneraci.

 - Dotované obědy & občerstvení zdarma – dobré jídlo, skvělá káva a čerstvé ovoce přímo na pracovišti každý den.

 - Příspěvek na ošatné – 86 Kč navíc ke každé odpracované směně.

 - Systém odměn za pochvaly – sbírání hvězdiček od kolegů a jejich výměna za vouchery do Alzy, Notina a dalších e-shopů.

 - Multisport karta – příspěvek na sport i zasloužený relax po práci.

 - Fajn firemní akce – společné oslavy úspěchů a neformální večírky.
   
   

Proč právě tahle práce?

Výsledek svojí práce uvidíš každý den. Pomáháš rozhodovat o tom, jaké zboží se dostane až k zákazníkovi. Když něco není v pořádku, máš možnost to zachytit dřív, než produkt opustí sklad.

Hledáme někoho, komu záleží na tom, aby věci byly udělané správně – protože právě díky takovým lidem můžeme zákazníkům doručovat potraviny v kvalitě, kterou od Rohlíku očekávají.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive, Privy
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Privy

Our mission is to make privacy and user ownership the default online. We build simple, flexible application programming interfaces (APIs) and tools that help developers create products on crypto infrastructure.

Privy provides the abstraction and infrastructure layer above wallets, integrating across blockchain networks, third-party providers, and Stripe products such as Treasury and Link. We solve complex technical problems while using Stripe’s global reach to support customers including Ramp, Klarna, Deel, Kraken, Hyperliquid, and Fomo. Our technology powers experiences for both mainstream users and crypto-native audiences.

Learn more: [Privy and Stripe: Bringing crypto to everyone]

About the team

The Account Executive, Product team connects Privy’s technology with companies building new products across fintech and crypto. The team works closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market partners to understand prospective customers’ needs, shape technical and commercial solutions, and turn market insights into product and sales strategy. Its focus includes priority segments such as neobanking, payments, and brokerages.

What you’ll do

As an Enterprise Account Executive you’ll own complex enterprise sales cycles and help expand Privy’s work with companies across fintech and crypto. You’ll build relationships with senior commercial and technical stakeholders, develop new opportunities, and help refine Privy’s enterprise sales approach. You’ll also contribute to Privy’s global growth strategy and represent the company at industry events.

Responsibilities

• Partner with the Head of Go-to-Market (GTM) to build and close a strong pipeline of enterprise prospects.

• Develop and test outbound campaigns based on market and customer feedback.

• Manage a pipeline across multiple ideal customer profiles.

• Build deep expertise in Privy’s products and lead discovery calls with fintech prospects to understand their needs and explain Privy’s value.

• Own the full sales cycle, from sourcing opportunities through contract close, and serve as the primary commercial contact for prospective customers.

• Contribute to the Go-to-Market team’s strategy across North America and other global markets, including Latin America, Asia, and Africa.

• Analyze market trends and emerging opportunities to inform Privy’s positioning and sales strategy.

• Represent Privy at industry events and conferences as a spokesperson for its fintech business.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 5 to 10 years of experience in sales, business development, or a related field, including experience selling a technical product and a record of strong performance.

• You have experience selling technical products within fintech, crypto, or a related industry. You can build a pipeline, lead complex sales cycles, and develop trusted relationships with commercial and technical stakeholders.

• Experience leading complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals involving legal, compliance, engineering, and other buyer-side teams through contract close.

• Ability to work effectively in an early-stage environment and build repeatable processes where none exist.

• Experience building strong networks within a specific industry, ideally fintech, payments, or crypto.

• Strong communication, negotiation, relationship management, and sales skills.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience selling API-first or developer-focused products.

• Ability to lead discovery conversations with technical buyers, including chief technology officers and product leaders.

• Familiarity with crypto infrastructure, such as stablecoins, on-ramps and off-ramps, wallets, and custody, or a demonstrated ability to learn the space quickly.

jobs.title: Early Years Practitioner
jobs.description:
arly Years Practitioner – Babyzone Everyday Maths & Nest

A rewarding, part-time educator role, ideal for early years or primary practitioners who are passionate about supporting families to build confidence in everyday maths, managing big feelings and the everyday moments in between.

About Babyzone

At Babyzone, we believe that every child deserves the strongest possible start in life, regardless of their background or circumstances. Our community-driven hubs provide warm, inclusive spaces where families feel welcomed, supported and confident.

This role delivers two of Babyzone's practical, research-informed sessions for parents and children aged 0–5:

• Everyday Maths helps parents and children build early mathematical understanding through play, interaction and daily routines, so families feel confident using maths naturally at home and in everyday life.

• Nest helps parents and children build social and emotional skills through play, connection and shared routines, so families feel more confident handling tantrums, staying calm under stress and building connection with their child.

Why This Role is Perfect for You

Are you an experienced early years or primary educator who enjoys working directly with families? Are you confident leading small groups and passionate about learning through play and relationship?

This role is particularly suited to practitioners seeking flexible, part-time work alongside other roles or commitments. It offers a meaningful opportunity to deliver two high-quality, curriculum-based programmes, bringing variety to each delivery day, while being part of a supportive, values-driven organisation.

The Opportunity

As an Early Years Practitioner, you will deliver both the Everyday Maths and Nest curricula at Babyzone [Hub] each week. On each delivery day you will lead up to five sessions: two to three Everyday Maths sessions and two to three Nest sessions. You will play a vital role in creating a warm, engaging and safe learning environment where parents, carers and children learn together, with the carer-child relationship at the centre of every session.

You will:

• Deliver the Everyday Maths and Nest curricula with fidelity, ensuring sessions follow each programme's intended structure, learning goals and ethos

• Model age-appropriate mathematical play and interactions in Everyday Maths sessions, building families' confidence to use maths in daily life

• Lead the fixed ritual elements of Nest sessions, such as the Hello Song, Feelings Map check-in and Goodbye Song, which give children a predictable and regulating structure across the programme

• Model calm, regulated adult presence, understanding that children borrow calm from the adults around them

• Make small, appropriate adjustments to delivery in response to the needs of local families while preserving core content

• Prepare thoroughly for each session, including completing the required online pre-delivery modules for both programmes on the Babyzone learning platform

• Create a warm, inclusive and supportive atmosphere where all families feel encouraged to participate, without ever requiring participation

• Manage group dynamics to maintain a calm, positive and engaging session environment

• Prioritise safeguarding, safety and wellbeing at all times, in line with Babyzone expectations

• Work collaboratively with the Hub Manager and wider Babyzone team to support smooth hub delivery and continuous improvement

• Support the set-up and breakdown of the Babyzone space, including moving between Everyday Maths and Nest resources during the day, and be available during hub hours (8:30am–3:00pm) on delivery days

• Maintain accurate attendance and session records, delivering up to five sessions per day with a maximum of ten families per Everyday Maths session and twelve families per Nest session

What You'll Need

We're looking for someone who:

• Has professional teaching experience with nursery, pre-primary or primary-aged children

• Has a strong understanding of early childhood development, learning through play, and social and emotional learning

• Is confident building trust and rapport with families from diverse backgrounds

• Communicates clearly and confidently with both adults and children

• Is reliable, organised and comfortable delivering two structured, curriculum-based programmes in the same day

• Has a strong awareness of safeguarding responsibilities and a commitment to safe practice

Personal Attributes

You will be someone who:

• Is deeply aligned with Babyzone's mission, values and way of working

• Brings warmth, kindness and respect to their work with families

• Is enthusiastic about early maths and children's emotional development, and passionate about supporting families' confidence

• Is reflective, open to feedback and committed to developing their practice

• Is dependable and excited to contribute to a positive Babyzone community setting

Role Details

• Location: Babyzone Grimsby, Horizon Youth Zone, Garth Lane, Grimsby North East Lincolnshire DN31 1RP

• Hours: 8:30am–3:00pm on delivery days (Fridays, term time only)

• Contract: Part-time, self-employed (professional indemnity and public liability insurance required)

• Pay: £200 per delivery day

• Start Date: 6th November 2026

• Reports to: Hub Manager / Programme Lead

What We Offer

• Full training on the Everyday Maths and Nest curricula and the Babyzone ethos

• A supportive team environment with ongoing coaching and guidance

• Flexible, part-time work that fits around other commitments

• The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on families' early learning and emotional development

jobs.title: Software Engineering Residency Program
jobs.description:
Software Engineering Residency Program

Program Duration: January 11 through March 31, 2027 (11.5 weeks). Residents work 40 hours per week, Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM with a 30-minute lunch.

Position Type: Temporary, Non-Exempt, Hourly

Conversion to Full-Time: This is the heart of the program: residents who successfully complete the residency may be eligible to join Bluestaq full-time as an Associate Software Engineer. Full-time offers are contingent on performance and business need.

Position Description
Ready to launch your software career? The Bluestaq Software Engineering Residency Program is an 11.5-week, paid, cohort-based program built around one goal: turning promising early-career developers into full-time Bluestaq Associate Software Engineers. This isn't a coffee-run internship. From week one you'll work real backlog items on the systems our U.S. Space Force customers use every day, guided by a dedicated engineer-mentor, and you'll close out the program by presenting your capstone work directly to Bluestaq engineering leadership.

Who We’re Looking For
We're offering the residency to early-career software talent ready to commit to a full-time engineering role, including: final-year undergraduate and master's students (graduating by January 2027), recent graduates in Computer Science, Mathematics, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related fields. If you're excited about learning fast, collaborating, and shipping real-world solutions, we want you on our team.

What You’ll Do
At Bluestaq, our residents aren't confined to one technology stack. You'll explore multiple technologies while contributing to impactful projects. Expect to work with languages and tools like Java, Python, Angular, Groovy, REST Services, GIT, PostgreSQL, Mongo, Athena, NiFi, Quarkus, and cloud platforms like Google Cloud, MS Azure, and AWS.

This isn't just about coding — we're all about growing your skills. You'll pair with experienced engineers, learn data storage solutions, front-end and back-end technologies, and cloud-based infrastructure, with structured milestones along the way: an onboarding week covering our tooling and secure development practices, a midpoint demo, and a capstone presentation. We offer the perfect balance of guidance and independence, allowing you to learn while making a real impact.

What Makes You a Great Fit

• You have software development experience through coursework, personal projects, bootcamp work, or prior internships.

• You have experience with software development and scripting languages.

• You're familiar with front-end/back-end technologies, data storage solutions, and cloud platforms like AWS, Google Cloud, or MS Azure.

• You're capable of working in a team-centric environment.

• You have excellent verbal and written communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

• You're passionate about big data technologies and excited to work with cloud infrastructures.

• You have ability to obtain a security clearance.

• You’re available to work full-time on-site for the full program (January 11 – March 31, 2027).

Benefits: This position is not eligible for employment benefits such as 401k, Medical, Dental, or Vision Insurance. This position is eligible for sick pay as per the Colorado Healthy Families & Workplaces Act (HFWA).

Salary Range (CO)

$40—$40 USD

Clearance Requirement: This position may require an active TS/SCI Clearance. Current clearance holders are strongly encouraged to apply. If you don't currently hold one, Bluestaq will sponsor eligible candidates through the clearance process based on program needs.

Relocation: Relocation assistance is available for full-time positions.

About Bluestaq
At Bluestaq, we build secure data platforms that matter for space missions, national defense, healthcare systems, and commercial innovation. Founded in 2018, we've become a leader in enterprise software and secure data management by staying focused on what counts: modern architecture, operational excellence, and mission impact.

We're engineers, problem-solvers, and builders who take the mission seriously, but not ourselves. We automate the repeatable, question the status quo, and design systems that are as reliable as they are scalable. Whether we're supporting space, defense systems, or healthcare advancements, we build with the same principles: cloud-native solutions, security by design, and relentless simplicity.

What We Offer:
For full-time positions

• 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision for you and your dependents

• 10% total 401(k) contribution from day one, no vesting period — Bluestaq contributes 4% automatically and matches 100% of the next 6%

• Every role is eligible for an annual performance bonus

• $200,000 employer-paid life insurance, plus short- and long-term disability coverage

• $5,000 annual professional development budget per employee

• 20 days PTO, plus 8 paid holidays

• Pet insurance, onsite gym, and flexible schedule

Bluestaq is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit unlawful discrimination against applicants or employees on the basis age 40 and over, color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, military or veteran status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by state or local law.

Bluestaq will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities and employees whose work requirements interfere with a religious belief unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to Bluestaq or a direct threat. Employees needing such accommodation are instructed to contact Human Resources immediately at contact.us@bluestaq.com.

Applications will be accepted for 60 days beyond the posting date, or until the position is filled, whichever comes first.

jobs.title: Technical Programme Manager, Manufacturing and Deployment
jobs.description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

We are looking for a Technical Programme Manager to lead global manufacturing programmes for IonQ's quantum computing systems and to own complex customer site deployments across the Americas. You will orchestrate worldwide subsystem manufacturing, with photonics and advanced electronics at the centre, and keep deployment programmes running to plan.

You will drive execution across engineering, science, global mobility, legal, supply chain, logistics, facilities, security and customer teams, so that advanced quantum systems are built, delivered, installed and commissioned successfully. The work suits someone comfortable in ambiguity, at ease with international programmes and their dependencies, and able to carry a site from early planning through onsite execution to customer handover.

What you will do

• Lead planning and execution of global quantum system manufacturing across every production facility.

• Lead deployment and commissioning at customer sites across the Americas, from planning through to handover.

• Work with research, production, compliance and logistics teams to keep builds and subassembly deliveries on schedule.

• Run site readiness with facilities, security, networking and customer stakeholders, and coordinate staffing, installation sequencing and vendors onsite.

• Manage risk, issues and escalation across internal teams, vendors and customers so that schedules hold.

What you will bring

You will have five or more years in technical programme management, manufacturing or deployment of complex hardware systems, alongside a technical degree or equivalent experience. You will have run international programmes that pulled together logistics, facilities, trade compliance, mobility and field operations, and you will be used to holding a critical path across teams that do not report to you. Clear written and spoken communication matters here, as does the confidence to decide when the picture is incomplete.

You'd be a great fit with

• Experience scaling high technology hardware factory operations across more than one continent.

• Familiarity with facilities buildout, infrastructure readiness or construction coordination for technical installations.

• Onsite deployment experience with enterprise, government or research customers.

• Exposure to trapped ion systems, photonics, quantum computing or comparable advanced hardware.

• An MS in physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering or a related technical field.

This role is based in Bothell, Washington, on site at least three days a week, with travel of around 30%, mostly within the United States, and occasional trips to our Oxford site.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

At IonQ, we believe in fair treatment, access, opportunity, and advancement for all while striving to identify and eliminate barriers. We empower employees to thrive by fostering a culture of autonomy, productivity, and respect. We are dedicated to creating an environment where individuals can feel welcomed, respected, supported, and valued.

We are committed to equity and justice. We welcome different voices and viewpoints and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, ancestry, physical and/or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. We are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

US Technical Jobs. The position you are applying for will require access to technology that is subject to U.S. export control and government contract restrictions.  Employment with IonQ is contingent on either verifying “U.S. Person” (e.g., U.S. citizen, U.S. national, U.S. permanent resident, or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum) status for export controls and government contracts work, obtaining any necessary license, and/or confirming the availability of a license exception under U.S. export controls.  Please note that in the absence of confirming you are a U.S. Person for export control and government contracts work purposes, IonQ may choose not to apply for a license or decline to use a license exception (if available) for you to access export-controlled technology that may require authorization, and similarly, you may not qualify for government contracts work that requires U.S. Persons, and IonQ may decline to proceed with your application on those bases alone.  Accordingly, we will have some additional questions regarding your immigration status that will be used for export control and compliance purposes, and the answers will be reviewed by compliance personnel to ensure compliance with federal law.

US Non-Technical Jobs. Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Accordingly, we will have some additional questions regarding your immigration status that will be used for export control and compliance purposes, and the answers will be reviewed by compliance personnel to ensure compliance with federal law.

If you are interested in being a part of our team and mission, we encourage you to apply!

jobs.title: Business Analyst ( Product Operations Specialist) ( 3 Month Contract)
jobs.description:
Business Analyst (Product Operations Specialist)

(3 month Fixed Term Role with scope to extend)

New York/ Remote US (with 2 days per week office time in New York)

Prolific

Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are the architects of the human data infrastructure that's reshaping the landscape of AI development. In a world where foundational AI technologies are increasingly commoditized, it's the quality and diversity of human-generated data that truly differentiates products and models.

The role

Prolific for AI takes on a wide and fast-moving range of customer projects across our biggest AI accounts. Every project has its own requirements, systems, and stakeholders – and right now, that complexity lives in people's heads rather than on paper. We're looking for a Business Analyst / Product Operations Manager to fix that.

You’ll get into the weeds of each project's requirements and systems, and turn that complexity into visual maps that the whole team can work from. You’ll be the person who steps back across them, spots the patterns, and tells us what's repeating, what's diverging, and what should become a reusable playbook.

You'll also own how requests reach the product team in the first place, building the internal intake process that determines how we become aware of, understand, and prioritise customer asks.

Impact: You'll bring order and visibility to a high-throughput, high-complexity part of the business. Every pilot you map makes the next one faster to run and easier to hand off.

Experience: You’ll come from a Product or Delivery or Operations background and have cross-functional skills. Building the plane while flying it should excite you, not scare you. You're comfortable being the person who asks the detailed questions until the system actually makes sense – and you know how to represent what you've learned so that other people can act on it immediately, without a meeting.

Domain: You'll sit within Prolific for AI, working across multiple customer projects at once – all of them among our biggest accounts. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Services teams who run these projects day to day.

Culture: Adding on to our Prolific Principles, we expect colleagues to demonstrate reliability, grit, diplomacy, a bias for action, and a dogged focus on value – you'll bring these behaviours to a role that only works if people trust your attention to detail and precision of communication.

What you’ll be doing in the role

• Own the internal customer request intake process – defining and running how the product team becomes aware of, understands, and triages incoming requests from across Prolific for AI's customer projects.

• Map the process flow for each customer project you support, getting into the detail of project requirements and systems.

• Produce clear, high-quality visual documentation of all kinds that make complicated data and processes easy for others to understand at a glance.

• Map and pattern-match across our pilot projects, surfacing what's common, what's diverging, and what should be templated or automated.

• Build out automations, connectors, and lightweight tooling that remove manual work from recurring processes.

• Work directly with the client-facing and product teams supporting our biggest AI accounts, translating messy, in-flight project detail into structure the team can act on.

What you’ll bring to the role

• Proven experience as a Business Analyst, Product Operations Manager, Delivery Manager or similar, ideally supporting multiple concurrent projects or customer accounts.

• A genuine strength – and enjoyment – in visualising complicated information: you find systems maps, journey maps, service blueprints, and actor maps a natural and satisfying way to think, not a chore.

• Comfort getting into the weeds of project requirements, and the diplomacy to do so across multiple stakeholders and customers at once.

• Experience designing or improving an intake/triage process, ideally for product teams.

• Practical experience with automations and connectors, and the instinct to reach for them when a process is repeatable.

Why Prolific is a great place to work

We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.

We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviors into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breath and the best of humanity.

Join us to enjoy a competitive salary, benefits, and remote working within our impactful, mission-driven culture. At Prolific, our compensation packages for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits. Many roles also include the opportunity to earn a cash variable element, such as a bonus or commission. Each job posting shows a salary range that reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hires, based on the role’s location as well as your skills, experience, and relevant education or training. You can check the job posting’s subtitle to see where the position is based. Your recruiter will also be happy to share the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

For pay transparency, the base salary range for this full-time role in New York is $125,000- $150,000 per annum.

Links to more information on Prolific

Website

Youtube

Privacy Statement

By submitting your application, you agree that Prolific may collect your personal data for recruiting and global organisation planning. Prolific's Candidate Privacy Notice explains what personal information Prolific may process, where Prolific may process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Prolific use of your personal information.

jobs.title: ANALISTA LOGISTICA JR
Vice President, Controller
jobs.description:
About ShiftKey

ShiftKey is a platform that is disrupting the way healthcare facilities find licensed and certified professionals to fill available shifts. Leveraging marketplace dynamics and deep industry knowledge, the company is playing a vital role in mitigating America’s healthcare staffing shortages, enabling direct connections between facilities and healthcare professionals. By offering the opportunity to work as much or as little as they choose and putting the power back into the hands of healthcare workers, ShiftKey is bringing more licensed professionals back into the workforce, a solution that is solving a major crisis in healthcare. For more information, visit www.ShiftKey.com http://www.ShiftKey.com.



The role

We're looking for a VP, Controller to lead our accounting organization - the person who owns the numbers, end to end. There's an established team and established processes already in place, so this isn't a build-it-from-scratch job. What we need is someone who can run that engine well, tighten it up where it's loose, and push it toward the next level of speed and scale. You'll own everything from the monthly close to internal controls to audit, leading through a team of managers and a director rather than doing it all yourself - and you're joining at a moment where clean, audit-ready books matter more than usual, so someone who's comfortable under that kind of scrutiny will thrive here.



Where you'll work

This is a hybrid position based at our HQ in Irving, Texas. You'll be expected to work from the office 3-4 days per week.



What you'll be doing

 - Lead the controllership organization - General Ledger, Accounts Receivable, vendor/provider disbursements, Tax, and Treasury - through an established team of a director and managers, working across all three functions rather than just one.

 - Own the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of financial reporting and the monthly close process, with a clear mandate to make it materially faster and cleaner.

 - Help prepare clean, audit-ready financials and support an upcoming external audit, with real urgency given the timing - you'll need to ramp quickly to add value from early on.

 - Partner with the AR team to bring days sales outstanding under control, and work with the product team to understand and resolve payment reliability issues on the provider side of our marketplace.

 - Strengthen internal controls, accounting policies, and overall financial discipline across the organization.

 - Drive process improvement and automation - including how we use our accounting systems and AI tools - to build more scalable operations.

 - Partner closely with senior finance and revenue leadership to flag risks, solve problems, and support key business decisions, and develop the leaders on your team.
   
    

What you'll need

 - CPA required.

 - 12+ years of progressive accounting experience, including meaningful senior leadership experience managing through directors/managers - not just individual contributors.

 - Deep technical accounting and US GAAP knowledge, paired with hands-on operational experience owning financial reporting, close, controls, and audit for a full accounting function.

 - Genuine openness to using AI in accounting workflows. 

 - A proven track record improving processes, controls, and systems at scale, ideally in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Strong ERP experience.

 - Strong executive presence and the ability to partner effectively with senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
   
    

Perks of working for ShiftKey

 - Inclusive and collaborative work environment where all voices are valued.

 - Hybrid-friendly office spaces designed to be fun and engaging.

 - Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage.

 - Benefits begin on your first day.

 - Generous PTO and company-paid holidays, including flexible floating holidays.

 - 100% 401(k) employer match up to 6%.

 - Paid parental leave.

 - Wellness support, including access to mental health resources.

#LI-Hybrid



Our Commitment to Diversity

ShiftKey is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to embracing diverse and individual perspectives shaping our culture and contributing to the solutions that transform the world. We actively work to create an inclusive environment for employees to thrive. 



EEO Statement

ShiftKey does not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.  ShiftKey is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to applicants with a mental or physical disability, please contact: accommodations@shiftkey.com

jobs.title: Senior Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Anduril Imaging team develops state-of-the-art imaging systems across both hardware and software, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The team is heavily involved in utilizing computer vision, perception, electro-optical, infrared, and sensor data to give our war fighters and allies an advantage.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a hands-on Systems Engineer to join our team as we transition a Ladar product from the Engineering Development Unit (EDU) phase through Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD), and ultimately into high-rate production.

You will play a pivotal role in scaling our build capacity to 10s of units per month. You will bridge the gap between design and manufacturing, lead rigorous testing campaigns, and help mature our hardware and software systems to achieve high Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) ahead of our upcoming Critical Design Review (CDR) and Manufacturing Readiness Review (MRR).

A successful candidate will have a strong background in Electro-Optical (EO) systems, precision pointing, and a passion for transitioning complex hardware from R&D to the production floor.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Drive the EDU-to-EMD Transition: Oversee the deployment and test of our EDU builds, ensuring they are fully prepared to support field testing to demonstrate system capability and performance.

• Lead Qualification & Testing: Design and execute a comprehensive Design Verification Testing (DVT) campaign to environmentally test and qualify the system.

• Prepare for Major Milestones: Author technical documentation, define verification matrices, and lead systems-level preparation for upcoming Critical Design Reviews (CDR) and Manufacturing Readiness Reviews (MRR).

• Scale for Production: Collaborate with manufacturing and hardware teams to implement Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles. Scale our production capabilities from a few units per year to a target volume of ~10s of systems per month.

• Optimize Test Infrastructure: Architect, design, and ruggedize manufacturing test equipment for efficiency, throughput, and reliability on the production floor.

• Automate & Integrate: Collaborate with software and firmware teams to implement robust test automation, while pushing the user interface (UI) and background software towards product-level maturity.

• Adapt or derive physics-based models of sensor system performance and derive requirements based on those models, and validate models against laboratory and real world data

• Support both laboratory-based and field-based experiments and demonstrations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• EO/Ladar Domain Expertise: 5+ years of hardware-centric systems engineering experience working with Electro-Optical (EO) systems, Ladar/Lidar, or high-precision pointing systems.

• Development-to-Production Experience: Direct experience transitioning complex, multidisciplinary systems from low Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) to high TRL / production-ready status.

• Testing & Environmental Qualification: Strong familiarity with DVT campaigns, environmental testing standards, and field testing operations.

• Production Scaling Mindset: Practical knowledge of Design for Manufacturing (DFM), test equipment ruggedization, and test process optimization/automation.

• Milestone Execution: Experience leading or heavily contributing to systems engineering reviews such as CDR, MRR, or PRR.

• Collaboration & Communication: Outstanding ability to communicate across multidisciplinary teams (optical, mechanical, electrical, firmware, software, and manufacturing).

• Advanced proficiency in an analytical toolchains/languages (e.g., MATLAB, Python)

• Strong laboratory skills (e.g. design of experiments)

• Willingness to travel to test sites.

• Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with software/hardware integration, specifically defining software interfaces, UI productization, and background software requirements.

• Experience with software/firmware automated test frameworks.

• Knowledge of current and next-generation advanced sensing systems and platforms

US Salary Range

jobs.description:

ABOUT THE JOB

As the Lead Hardware Engineer for our ladar product line, you will be responsible for the domain-specific detailed technical execution, hardware architecture, and engineering execution across all hardware disciplines (mechanical, electrical, optical, and test). You will transition our high-precision active electro-optical (EO) systems from early-stage prototypes and Engineering Development Units (EDUs) through Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD), and ultimately into scaled, high-rate production.

Anduril Imaging Hardware Lead Engineers are responsible for hardware architecture, development execution, and overall technical strategy for land, sea, air, and space EO/IR applications. In this role, you will lead trade studies to define EO/IR system architectures, lead the multidisciplinary detailed design, analysis, and integration and test of EO/IR prototypes and products. You will lead a small team of engineers from concept ideation through system definition and development. You will carry products in your portfolio through NPI into production, and have overall oversight in to hardware sustainment and evolutionary development activities. You will help shape internal and external investment priorities to grow the scope and impact of your product family.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Define the "How" of Hardware: Own domain-specific hardware architecture, component selection, physical design, and detailed mechanical, electrical, optical, and test engineering.

• Transition and Scale Production: Lead the critical transition of our hardware from low-volume, hard-to-build prototype units to a high-rate EMD production environment.

• Deliver Major Milestones: Lead hardware preparation, technical artifacts, and clear-to-build criteria for upcoming program milestones, including Hardware SRR, PDR, CDR, and Manufacturing Readiness Reviews (MRR).

• Manage EMD & NPI Builds: Own the hardware side of New Product Introduction (NPI). Coordinate, inventory, and lead the assembly of final EDU and EMD-1 builds, ensuring they are ready for field testing and environmental Design Verification Testing (DVT).

• Design & Ruggedize Test Equipment: Architect, build, and ruggedize manufacturing and optical test equipment to ensure highly efficient, repeatable, and automated testing on the production floor.

• Define V+V Metrics: Define, implement, and track hardware Verification and Validation (V+V) metrics Lead HW to ensure absolute system reliability in extreme physical environments.

• Staffing & Collaboration: Partner closely with the Chief Engineer. Work directly with functional engineering leads to ensure your product line has sufficient, high-performing hardware engineering staffing.

• Hardware Sustainment: Own the detailed hardware Continuous Improvement (CI) roadmap, oversee the hardware Configuration Control/Change Review Board (CRB), and drive rapid resolution of hardware field issues

• Education: Degree in a technical field such as mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, optical engineering, systems engineering, physics, or a hard science.

• Experience: 8+ years of experience developing and deploying complex electromechanical, electro-optical, or active sensing systems.

• Technical Breadth: Deep engineering skillset spanning mechanical, electrical, optical, and test disciplines, with proven experience performing system design, architecture definition, and performance modeling.

• NPI & Scale Experience: Proven experience managing New Product Introduction (NPI), leading initial system builds, and managing hardware scaling or sustainment at scale.

• Leadership: Strong track record of leading high-performance, cross-functional engineering teams in a fast-paced environment.

• Travel: Willingness to travel to test sites and manufacturing facilities as needed.

• Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Ladar/EO Domain Expertise: Direct experience defining, designing, and testing active optical/imaging systems, Ladar/Lidar, or high-precision pointing architectures.

• TRL Transition Experience: Proven success transitioning hardware from low Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) / rapid prototyping environments to high-reliability, qualified EMD and production programs.

• Testing & DVT: Strong hands-on experience with environmental testing standards (thermal, shock, vibration) and using advanced design, simulation, and optical test equipment.

• Supply Chain and Operations: Familiarity with supply chain coordination, inventory management, and defining "clear to build" metrics for complex assemblies.

jobs.title: Clinical Trial Manager (Contract)
jobs.description:
Centessa Pharmaceuticals, a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company, is a clinical-stage company developing orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonists as a new class of medicines for the treatment of narcolepsy and potentially other sleep-wake disorders. Centessa’s lead investigational candidate – cleminorexton (formerly ORX750) – is being developed for narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2, and idiopathic hypersomnia. Centessa's OX2R agonist portfolio includes additional clinical and preclinical-stage assets with potential utility across a broader range of neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuropsychiatric conditions.

Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, Centessa was recognized as a Great Place to Work® in 2026.

Description of Role

Centessa is seeking a (contract to hire) Clinical Trial Manager to lead the execution of mid‑ to late‑stage global clinical studies from study start‑up through close‑out and clinical study report. This role is a temporary position with the potential to convert to a permanent role, responsible for day‑to‑day trial management, coordinating internal cross‑functional teams and overseeing CROs and external vendors to ensure studies are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with quality and regulatory standards. This role requires hands‑on involvement in clinical trial execution, proactive identification and resolution of operational issues, and accountability for study performance metrics and deliverable quality. The CTM also contributes to operational planning, risk assessment, and continuous process improvement in collaboration with study team leadership.

Key Responsibilities

• Plan and execute mid‑ to late‑stage CNS clinical trials from study start‑up through close‑out, ensuring operational excellence, high data quality, and compliance with protocol, GCP, and global regulatory requirements.

• Lead day‑to‑day clinical trial operations, coordinating cross‑functional partners (Clinical Development, Data Management, Biostatistics, Regulatory, Safety) to ensure efficient trial execution and alignment to program objectives.

• Oversee CROs and external vendors supporting CNS clinical trials, including co‑monitoring activities, to ensure delivery against scope of work, timelines, budget, and quality expectations.

• Drive critical study milestones, including site activation, enrollment progress, patient retention, data cleaning, and database lock, proactively addressing operational challenges common to CNS trials.

• Review and approve CRO‑ and vendor‑generated plans and study documentation, ensuring alignment with protocol, regulatory expectations, and Centessa quality standards.

• Monitor study progress and performance using operational metrics and tools, maintaining dashboards, timelines, and financial tracking, and providing clear, timely status updates to study teams and management.

• Identify, assess, and manage operational risks, proposing practical mitigation strategies and supporting informed decision‑making to minimize impact to timelines, quality, and patient safety.

• Ensure inspection and audit readiness, including oversight of Trial Master File (TMF) set‑up, ongoing maintenance, and close‑out for CNS studies.

• Contribute to operational planning and regulatory deliverables, supporting preparation of study‑level documentation for Health Authority interactions and continuous improvement of clinical operations processes.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or health‑related discipline.

• 5+ years clinical trial management experience within an industry sponsor environment, supporting drug development programs.

• Experience managing clinical trials in CNS therapeutic development strongly preferred.

• Proven ability to manage global clinical studies, including coordination with investigators, CROs, and functional vendors.

• Strong working knowledge of ICH guidelines, GCP, and global regulatory requirements applicable to clinical trials.

• Solid understanding of project management principles, including planning and managing timelines, resources, budgets, and risk–benefit trade‑offs; PMP or similar training is a plus.

• Excellent communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence without formal authority and drive cross‑functional team performance.

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment, meeting aggressive timelines while maintaining quality.

• Proactive problem‑solving mindset with the ability to anticipate issues, identify creative solutions, and take initiative to address risks impacting timelines or budgets.

Compensation

The hourly range for this position is $65.00 to $90.00 per hour. Individual compensation within this range will be determined based on a variety of factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, and job knowledge.

Contractors engaged through Centessa are employed through a third-party agency that serves as the employer of record and provides access to a comprehensive benefits package. Eligible contractors may enroll in medical plans, including PPO and EPO options, as well as dental and vision coverage after 30 days. Additional perks, such as a 401(k), wellness programs, and other discounts, may also be available to eligible contractors.

Work Location

The (contract-to-hire) Clinical Trial Manager role is a remote role based in the US.

POSITION: Temporary, non-exempt

We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

Please note: We will not assign referral rights for any unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies.

jobs.description:
ABOUT HANDSHAKE

Handshake was founded on a simple belief that everyone deserves a path to a great career, regardless of where they went to school or who they know. Today, we power 25 million job seekers, 1 million+ employers, and 1,600 educational institutions.

In 2025, we started Handshake AI and built the fastest-growing AI data business in history. We work directly with frontier AI lab researchers to create evaluations, publish benchmarks, and push the boundary of data. We’ve grown from $0 to ~$1B run rate and pay ~$60M to over 30K individuals every month.




WHY JOIN HANDSHAKE NOW:

 - Shape how every career evolves in the AI economy, at global scale, with impact your friends, family and peers can see and feel

 - Partner hand-in-hand with world-class AI labs, Fortune 500 partners and the world’s top educational institutions

 - Work together with engineers, scientists, operators, and more from Palantir, Meta, Scale AI, and former YC founders

 - Build a massive, fast-growing business with billions in revenue




ABOUT THE ROLE

Handshake puts the customer at the center of everything we do. Our Customer Success team is the secret to making that a reality. The Customer Success team is passionate about helping recruiters become more efficient, and are the driving force for the organizational change that helps our customers realize the full potential of Handshake.



The Customer Success Manager plays a crucial role in ensuring the success and satisfaction of our customers. This role involves developing strong relationships with customers, understanding their business needs, and proactively working to drive value and maximize their return on investment. The Customer Success Manager serves as a liaison between the customer and various internal teams, advocating for the customer's needs and helping to identify opportunities for growth. In this role you will:



 - Manage portfolio of roughly 60-75 accounts in our Commercial segment (SMB and Midmarket companies with <2500 employees).

 - Own customer onboarding, ensuring a seamless transition to our products or services.

 - Drive product adoption of Handshake through on-going guidance and training that align with each customer’s needs and objectives.

 - Build and nurture strong, relationships with various personas on the customer side; including Directors and above.

 - Develop and execute customer success plans, proactively identifying and mitigating churn risk, tracking progress, and adjusting as needed.

 - Run and maintain regular customer calls and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).

 - Identify opportunities for upselling and cross-selling and surface these to Account Manager.

 - Collect customer feedback to advocate for their needs within the organization, collaborating with Product & Engineering to drive product improvement and enhancement.

 - Ensure customer renewals by demonstrating sustained value and partnering with Account Managers during the renewal process.

 - Take a proactive role in optimizing existing or building new processes & assets that enable the team to scale.




YOU HAVE

 - 3+ years in Customer Success, Account Management or Consulting.

 - 5+ years work experience.

 - Strong business acumen and deep knowledge of Customer Success practices.

 - Customer-centric mindset.

 - Exceptional presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.

 - Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional team.

 - Analytical and data-driven thinker with the ability to collect, organize, analyze, and accurately summarize significant amounts of information to senior-level stakeholders.

 - Quick and agile work style with strong attention to detail.

 - Self-motivated with a positive attitude and excitement for work.

 - Comfortable learning and working in a start-up environment.

 - Experience in SaaS start-up a plus.

 - Experience in Recruiting a plus.




WE OFFER

Handshake delivers benefits that help you feel supported and thrive at work and in life.

The below benefits are for full-time US employees.

🎯 Ownership: Equity in a fast-growing company
💰 Financial Wellness: 401(k) match, competitive compensation, financial coaching
🍼 Family Support: Paid parental leave, fertility benefits, parental coaching
💝 Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision, mental health support, $500 wellness stipend
📚 Growth: $2,000 learning stipend, ongoing development
💻 Remote & Office: Internet, commuting, and free lunch/gym in our SF office
🏝 Time Off: Flexible PTO, 15 holidays + 2 flex days
🤝 Connection: Team outings & referral bonuses

jobs.title: Customer Experience Coordinator - Leesburg, VA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Customer Experience Coordinator, your job is to define the customer’s experience through service, focus, and participation—so, you are passionate about perfecting the experience before, during, and after their time at VEG. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say yes and put patient and customer experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online

• Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly

• Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs

• Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate

• Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.

• Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions

• Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information

• Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships

• Celebrate and capture special moments (with permission), creating lasting connections between customers, their pets, and the hospital

WHAT YOU NEED

• 2+ years of experience in a customer service role

• Advanced knowledge in computer programs and practice management software

• Highly organized, with strong attention to detail

• A strong communicator; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone

• A strong multitasker, able to thrive amid chaos

• High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly

• Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.
