jobs.title: Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer to join our Operations Engineering team.

Position Description

The Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer supports the planning, coordination, and field execution of commissioning and startup activities for Oklo facilities. This role helps transition systems and facilities from construction through testing, turnover, operational readiness, initial operation, and project completion.

The Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer works directly with Operations, Engineering, Construction, Maintenance, Quality, Safety, vendors, contractors, and other project organizations to ensure systems are properly scoped, tested, documented, accepted, and ready for operation. This engineer develops and reviews commissioning plans, test procedures, system turnover requirements, schedules, resource needs, and readiness criteria and then provides onsite engineering support during execution.

During field assignments, the Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer may serve as a system-based commissioning engineer, test engineer, shift test engineer, or field engineering lead. The engineer confirms system and test readiness, supports test teams, monitors plant response and test data, coordinates troubleshooting, resolves deficiencies, and ensures results are properly evaluated and documented.

This is a project-deployment role with remote work between field assignments. When assigned to an active commissioning or startup project, the Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer must be prepared to mobilize to the applicable project site for periods lasting several weeks to several months. Upon completion of an assignment, the engineer may return to remote work until mobilized for the next project. The frequency, location, and duration of assignments will vary based on company and project needs.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Develop and implement commissioning and startup plans, strategies, schedules, system-based work scopes, and execution methods

• Define commissioning boundaries, test objectives, prerequisites, acceptance criteria, required resources, and system turnover requirements

• Develop, review, verify, and maintain preoperational, commissioning, integrated, and startup test procedures

• Translate design requirements, safety requirements, specifications, calculations, vendor information, and system requirements into executable test methods and acceptance criteria

• Develop and maintain commissioning test matrices, requirements-traceability tools, system status records, turnover packages, and test completion documentation

• Support systemization and define the structures, systems, components, boundaries, and work packages needed for effective commissioning and turnover

• Coordinate construction completion, system walkdowns, punch-list resolution, turnover documentation, and acceptance of systems for testing

• Verify test prerequisites, plant configuration, test boundaries, equipment status, temporary configurations, instrumentation, personnel, and procedural readiness before test execution

• Participate in pre-job briefs, daily coordination meetings, shift turnovers, schedule reviews, and test-readiness reviews

• Provide field engineering oversight during commissioning and startup testing

• Monitor system response and test data in real time and compare observed performance against expected results and acceptance criteria

• Support operators and test directors during system manipulations, integrated testing, startup testing, and other significant plant evolutions

• Identify unexpected conditions, emerging risks, procedure deficiencies, equipment problems, and adverse trends during field activities

• Exercise stop-work responsibility when testing cannot be performed safely or within approved requirements and controls

• Coordinate troubleshooting among Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Construction, vendors, contractors, and other technical organizations

• Document test deficiencies, open items, nonconformances, corrective actions, retest requirements, and final dispositions

• Evaluate test results and prepare or support test reports, completion packages, turnover records, and recommendations for system acceptance

• Support the transition from component-level testing to system testing, integrated plant testing, startup testing, and operational acceptance

• Coordinate vendor and contractor testing and ensure activities are aligned with Oklo requirements, facility configuration, work controls, and project schedules

• Support development and implementation of work-control, tagging, lockout/tagout, foreign-material-exclusion, configuration-control, and equipment-status-control practices needed during commissioning

• Participate in operational-readiness reviews, management assessments, inspections, audits, and resolution of readiness findings

• Provide input to operating procedures, maintenance procedures, training materials, system descriptions, and operational programs based on commissioning and startup experience

• Capture lessons learned and use field experience to improve future test procedures, commissioning methods, plant designs, and repeatable deployment practices

• Support multiple Oklo projects and facilities as priorities, schedules, and project phases evolve

• Qualify as an Oklo plant operator or complete other assigned technical qualifications, as applicable

• Maintain awareness of fast-reactor design, commissioning methods, operating experience, testing practices, and relevant industry developments

Minimum Qualifications:

At minimum, we are looking for:

• Bachelor’s degree in nuclear, mechanical, electrical, chemical, or another relevant engineering or technical discipline; equivalent directly applicable nuclear, commissioning, or operational experience may be considered in lieu of a degree

• Five or more years of experience in commissioning and startup, nuclear operations, system testing, field engineering, power generation, naval nuclear propulsion, national laboratory operations, construction completion, or another highly regulated technical environment

• Hands-on field experience supporting the testing, commissioning, startup, operation, maintenance, or troubleshooting of complex mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and controls, or process systems

• Experience developing, reviewing, or executing technical test procedures, commissioning procedures, operating procedures, or similar controlled work instructions

• Experience translating design requirements, specifications, calculations, safety requirements, or vendor information into executable tests and acceptance criteria

• Experience reading and interpreting technical documents such as piping and instrumentation diagrams, electrical single-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, logic diagrams, control narratives, system descriptions, specifications, calculations, and vendor manuals

• Working knowledge of system turnover, configuration control, work control, equipment status, test boundaries, and safe field execution

• Ability to evaluate system performance, interpret test data, identify abnormal conditions, and coordinate technical problem-solving in the field

• Demonstrated ability to work across Operations, Engineering, Construction, Maintenance, Quality, Safety, vendors, and contractors

• Strong technical writing, verbal communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills

• Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in dynamic field conditions using incomplete or evolving information

• Ability and willingness to mobilize to project sites for extended assignments lasting several weeks to several months

• Ability to work shifts, extended hours, nights, weekends, or holidays as required during commissioning and startup activities

• Ability to travel to Oklo facilities, national laboratories, vendor facilities, and other project locations as business needs require

• Ability to obtain and maintain unescorted access to nuclear facilities, if required

Bonus Qualifications:

Nice-to-haves include:

• Experience commissioning or starting up a nuclear facility, power plant, first-of-a-kind industrial facility, research reactor, microreactor, or Department of Energy nuclear facility

• Experience as a reactor operator, senior reactor operator, shift technical advisor, test engineer, system operator, engineering watchstander, or other nuclear facility operator

• Current or previous NRC Reactor Operator or Senior Reactor Operator license or certification

• Relevant qualification through the U.S. Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program, such as Engineering Officer of the Watch, Propulsion Plant Watch Officer, or Engineering Watch Supervisor

• Experience with sodium-cooled fast reactors, liquid-metal systems, fast-reactor technology, or sodium-system testing

• Experience with steam plants, heat-transport systems, electrical distribution, instrumentation and controls, digital control systems, or balance-of-plant systems

• Experience with systemization, construction completion, walkdowns, punch lists, turnover packages, completions-management software, or system acceptance

• Experience developing or executing preoperational, integrated, startup, surveillance, or acceptance testing

• Experience serving as a commissioning engineer, startup engineer, test engineer, shift test engineer, test director, or system-based commissioning lead

• Experience supporting joint test groups, test-review boards, readiness reviews, or other formal test-governance organizations

• Experience overseeing vendor or contractor testing and coordinating multi-organization field activities

• Experience with troubleshooting, root-cause evaluation, corrective-action programs, nonconformance resolution, or retesting

• Experience implementing work control, tagging, lockout/tagout, foreign-material-exclusion, configuration-control, or equipment-status-control programs

• Familiarity with applicable NRC requirements, Department of Energy requirements, industry standards, and nuclear safety and quality-assurance programs

• Experience working under a nuclear quality-assurance program

• Experience with field data collection, test instrumentation, data trending, test-result evaluation, and technical report preparation

• Experience working with regulators, national laboratories, construction contractors, vendors, customers, or other external technical stakeholders

Competencies

We are looking for a Nuclear Commissioning and Startup Engineer who is:

• Field-oriented and comfortable working directly with equipment, operators, technicians, contractors, and test teams

• A systems thinker who understands how individual components and systems interact as an integrated facility

• Able to convert design requirements and technical information into safe, practical, and executable field activities

• Disciplined in confirming prerequisites, boundaries, plant configuration, procedural compliance, and acceptance criteria

• Calm and methodical when responding to unexpected test results, equipment problems, changing conditions, and schedule pressure

• Willing to stop work, ask questions, and resolve uncertainty before proceeding

• Technically rigorous while remaining practical and focused on safe execution and project completion

• Comfortable moving between planning, procedure development, field execution, troubleshooting, data evaluation, and final documentation

• Able to coordinate multidisciplinary teams and maintain clear communication during complex or high-risk activities

• Prepared to live and work near project sites for extended periods while supporting major commissioning and startup campaigns

• Able to adapt between intensive field assignments and remote planning work as project needs evolve

• Passionate about clean energy

• An optimist at heart

• Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

• Willing and able to learn quickly

• Willing to think differently and do things in new ways

• Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment

• Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving while not leaning only on what has been done before

• Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems

• An excellent writer who can write in a modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!

• Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $1350,000-$185,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

jobs.title: Nuclear Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Nuclear Operations Engineer to join our Operations Engineering team.

Position Description

The Nuclear Operations Engineer supports the development and implementation of the operational capabilities needed to safely commission, start up, and operate Oklo facilities. This role translates plant designs, safety requirements, and program requirements into practical methods for operating the plant and conducting operational work.

The Nuclear Operations Engineer helps develop operational programs and the procedures used to implement those programs. The role also provides technical and operational input for normal, general, abnormal, emergency, surveillance, alarm-response, and administrative operating procedures. Working with procedure writers, system engineers, and other subject-matter experts, this engineer helps ensure procedures are technically accurate, operationally practical, and aligned with plant design and program requirements.

This role also supports system turnover, testing, commissioning, startup, and operational-readiness activities across Oklo projects. jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo!  We are searching for a Thermal-Hydraulics and Safety Analysis Engineer to join our isotope engineering team to own the thermal hydraulic safety case for the next generation of domestic isotope production facilities.

Position Description

The Thermal-Hydraulics and Safety Analysis Engineer is responsible for developing and executing systems-level thermal-hydraulic analyses that support the safety case, design basis, and licensing of Oklo's reactor systems. This engineer will evaluate reactor and plant response during normal operation, anticipated operational occurrences, and postulated accident conditions using codes such as RELAP5 and other systems-analysis tools.

This role combines hands-on transient modeling with safety-methodology development. The engineer will establish modeling approaches, assess code and model applicability, quantify uncertainty, and produce clear, auditable technical documentation suitable for licensing applications and regulatory review. The engineer will work closely with safety, licensing, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, controls, and system-design teams to connect analysis assumptions and acceptance criteria to an evolving reactor design.

This position is focused on thermal-hydraulic safety analysis and licensing support. It does not own source-term, radiological-consequence, or severe-accident progression analysis, although collaboration with engineers performing those analyses may be required.

The isotope engineering team is a small but growing team, so the candidate must be capable of operating in a highly iterative and independent environment.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Develop, maintain, and execute systems-level thermal-hydraulic models of reactor and plant behavior using RELAP5 or comparable analysis codes.

• Analyze normal operating conditions, anticipated operational occurrences, design-basis events, and selected beyond-design-basis conditions relevant to the thermal-hydraulic safety case.

• Develop event-specific analysis plans, including initial and boundary conditions, assumptions, acceptance criteria, figures of merit, and treatment of uncertainties.

• Develop and document thermal-hydraulic safety-analysis methods, modeling guidance, and engineering practices appropriate to advanced reactor licensing.

• Establish and justify code, model, and correlation applicability for the physical phenomena and operating regimes being evaluated.

• Perform model verification, validation, sensitivity studies, uncertainty analyses, scaling evaluations, and comparisons with experiments, benchmarks, hand calculations, or higher-fidelity analyses. Identify gaps in available methods, data, and validation evidence, and define practical plans to close those gaps.

• Translate regulatory requirements and safety acceptance criteria into defensible analysis requirements and technical evaluation strategies.

• Prepare high-quality calculation packages, methodology documents, safety-analysis reports, licensing-application content, and responses to regulator questions.

• Evaluate design changes and provide timely feedback on their effects on transient response, safety margins, system performance, and the licensing basis.

• Collaborate with reactor physics, fuel, controls, mechanical, thermal-hydraulics, safety, and licensing engineers on coupled analyses and interface conditions.

• Develop scripts and automated workflows for model generation, execution, post-processing, regression testing, and configuration control.

• Review safety analyses and models prepared by internal contributors, vendors, and external partners.

• Experience with verification and validation, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, scaling, bias evaluation, or code applicability assessments.

• Familiarity with experiment design, separate-effects and integral-effects testing, benchmark problems, and the use of test data to validate analytical methods.

• Fluency with Python or another language used for model automation, data analysis, visualization, and quality checks.

• Competency with modern software engineering practices, including version control, automated testing, reproducible computing environments, and continuous integration.

• Experience mentoring other analysts or providing technical review of safety-analysis work.

Competencies

• Methodical about verification, validation, uncertainty, configuration control, and technical documentation.

jobs.title: Senior/Lead Product Manager - Professional Trading Tools & Experience
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for a Senior or Lead Product Manager to lead the strategy, development, and continuous improvement of our professional trading tools and end-to-end trading experience.

This role is focused on products for active and professional traders. The scope includes advanced market analysis, trading workflows, order execution, position and risk management, workspace customisation, and selected automation capabilities.

You will develop a deep understanding of how professional traders use leading platforms such as TradingView, 3Commas, Bookmap, ATAS, and Quantower, and translate those insights into a differentiated, reliable, and intuitive trading experience.

Experience in the crypto industry is a strong plus. We welcome candidates who have built professional trading products for equities, futures, options, FX, commodities, or other electronic markets. Experience with crypto markets and products is a strong advantage.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and delivery of professional trading tools and the broader trading experience.

• Build a deep understanding of active and professional traders, including their daily workflows, trading behaviours, pain points, and expectations.

• Lead the development and improvement of market analysis, charting, order execution, position management, account monitoring, and workspace customisation.

• Identify opportunities to introduce advanced trading and automation capabilities that improve efficiency while keeping users in control of their trading decisions.

• Improve the quality of the end-to-end trading journey, from discovering an opportunity and placing an order through execution, position monitoring, and post-trade review.

• Ensure the product meets professional standards for performance, stability, accuracy, usability, and transparency, particularly during periods of high market volatility.

• Conduct structured user research and competitor analysis across professional trading terminals, charting platforms, and trading automation products.

• Define product success metrics and use customer feedback, behavioural data, and trading data to evaluate performance and guide priorities.

• Work closely with engineering, design, data, quantitative research, risk, compliance, operations, customer support, and commercial teams.

• Translate complex trader needs and market concepts into clear product requirements and intuitive user experiences.

• Manage technical and commercial trade-offs, dependencies, and delivery risks across multiple teams and product areas.

• Communicate product strategy, priorities, and outcomes clearly to senior stakeholders and distributed teams.

• Support and mentor other product managers and contribute to the broader trading product strategy

What We Look For In You

• 5-7+ years of product management experience, with a strong track record of delivering complex user-facing products.

jobs.title: Area Controller Europe South
jobs.description:
Join us in a pivotal area finance leadership role with responsibility across Spain, Portugal, Italy, and France. This position offers the opportunity to steer financial performance, strengthen governance, and act as a trusted partner to senior management. You will play a crucial role in harmonizing standards and elevating finance capabilities across the Area. The role is located in any of the 4 countries in the Area: Spain, France, Italy or Portugal.

• The Area Controller Europe South is responsible for the financial governance, performance oversight, and technical leadership of the Finance organizations across the Europe South Area (Spain, Portugal, Italy, and France).
• Operating as a regional finance leader, the role ensures consistency, quality, and compliance of financial reporting, controlling standards, and governance across countries, while acting as a key business partner and sparring partner to the Area Manager. The role is co-responsible for the financial performance of the Area and acts as a quality gate between local entities and EMEA / Group Finance.

Key Responsibilities

Area Financial Performance & Governance

• Oversee and challenge the financial performance of the Europe South countries, with a strong focus on Sales, Material Margin, Opex, EBITDA, and ONWC.
• Act as a quality gate for financial information reported from countries to Area, EMEA, and Group, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and transparency.
• Identify financial risks, deviations, and red flags across countries and escalate when required, acting as a link between local management and EMEA / Group Finance.
• Ensure alignment of local financial practices with Group, EMEA, and Area Europe South standards and policies.

Business Partnership at Area Level

• Act as the primary financial partner and sparring partner to the Area Manager.
• Actively contribute to Area management decisions as part of the Area leadership trio (Area GM, Area HR, Area Finance).
• Challenge business assumptions, performance drivers, and action plans with fact-based and data-driven analysis.
• Support strategic initiatives, restructuring topics, and performance improvement programs at Area level.

Governance of Local Finance Managers

• Provide functional leadership and technical guidance to local Finance Managers in Europe South, particularly on accounting, controlling, and financial governance topics where local General Managers may lack technical depth.
• Ensure local statutory, tax, treasury, and governance topics are properly managed, being informed and involved in key decisions while maintaining local accountability.
• Act as a reference point and escalation level for complex financial, accounting, tax, and audit-related matters.
• Promote consistent application of finance standards and best practices across countries.

Planning, Forecasting & Benchmarking

• Oversee and challenge country budgets, forecasts, and long-term plans, ensuring coherence at Area level.
• Define benchmarks, performance comparisons, and best practices across Europe South to foster continuous improvement.
• Support countries in translating benchmarks and insights into concrete action plans.

Compliance, Internal Controls & Audit Oversight

• Ensure a strong culture of governance, compliance, and internal controls across the Area.
• Oversee and support countries in internal and external audit processes, ensuring issues are addressed consistently and timely.
• Ensure alignment with Group and EMEA governance requirements, acting as an early warning system for compliance risks.

Finance Organization & Talent

• Shape and develop the finance organization across Europe South.
• Support definition of roles, succession planning, and identification of key talents within local finance teams.
• Promote knowledge sharing, capability building, and professional development of Finance Managers and their teams.

• Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field is a must
• 10+ years of experience in finance, controlling, or financial management, ideally in an international or multi‑country environment.
• Proven track record in regional or area financial leadership roles, preferably in matrix organizations.
• Strong technical background in accounting (IFRS preferred), controlling, and financial governance.
• Deep understanding of financial statements, KPIs, and performance drivers (Sales, Margin, Opex, EBITDA, ONWC).
• Strong expertise in planning, budgeting, forecasting, and financial modelling.

• Comfortable working with complex data sets and generating insight-driven analysis.

• Demonstrated experience developing finance teams across multiple countries.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, able to act as a sparring partner to senior leadership.
• Experience navigating complex organizational structures and balancing local vs. regional vs. group priorities.
• Strong understanding of commercial drivers and ability to link operational performance to financial impact.
• Experience supporting transformation, restructuring, and performance improvement initiatives.

We’re backed by Y Combinator and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. We’ve raised more than $100 million, including a $35 million Series A led by Accel.

We're looking for a strategic, well-connected partnerships leader to build our venture capital partnerships function from the ground up. You'll design and run a scalable program that engages venture firms, VC-backed companies, and the broader startup ecosystem. You'll work closely with our Head of PE & VC Practice, who will support you as you build the function.

The ideal candidate has already built a VC partnerships role or program from scratch, ideally at a technology startup. Experience selling or partnering around Office of the CFO technology is a strong plus.

What You'll Do

 - Design, launch, and own our VC partnerships strategy.

 - Build senior relationships with venture capital firms, accelerators, and other startup ecosystem partners.

 - Build repeatable ways to source and manage opportunities from VC partners, including referral processes, partner enablement, reporting, and feedback loops.

 - Host and run our own VC events, and represent the company at industry events, investor meetings, portfolio company forums, and ecosystem gatherings.

 - Track market trends, investment activity, and emerging companies to spot strategic opportunities and inform internal decisions.

What You'll Bring

 - 3–7 years of experience in partnerships, business development, venture capital, startup ecosystems, strategic alliances, or a related commercial role.

 - Proven experience taking a VC partnerships role, function, or program from zero to a repeatable operating model.

jobs.title: VP, Product
jobs.description:
At IQM, we build world-leading quantum computers for the well-being of humankind. We design systems to tackle computational challenges beyond the practical limits of classical machines. Our work sits at the edge of science and engineering. It's complex, demanding, and deeply collaborative. We turn deep research into reliable, full-stack systems that drive discoveries in fields like medicine, energy, and technology, reshaping how the world computes.

Join the team that gives quantum a heartbeat.

The work

Quantum computers are moving out of the lab and into real industrial use, and someone has to decide what we will build next. As VP of Product, that someone is you. You will turn IQM's technical milestones and R&D breakthroughs into a product roadmap that makes sense for cloud providers, HPC centers, system integrators, and sovereign cloud initiatives around the world. You will lead our product team and work closely with Technology and Commercial leadership. This is a role for someone who wants to shape how quantum computing becomes a practical, scalable industry, while it's still being defined.

We are looking for someone action oriented and hands-on where it counts, who puts IQM's success as the north start while still investing in the team around them.

What you’ll actually do

• Translate IQM's technical and R&D milestones into a clear, scalable product roadmap which is built together with internal stakeholders, including Technology teams
• Own product governance across our on-premises hardware, software, integration, and cloud offerings
• Lead and build high performing Product team, by developing individual growth
• Guide the shift from NISQ era research systems toward industrial QEC and FTQC systems
• Identify new market opportunities, industries and customer segments for our products in close partnership with Sales and Commercial teams, as the roadmap needs to be grounded in real customer demand
• Partner with executive leadership on strategic prioritization and budget planning
• Balance customer requirements, technical feasibility, and long-term strategy in every product decision
• Represent IQM at global summits, industry events, and executive level forums

What we’re looking for

• A Master's or PhD in engineering, physics, computer science, business, or a related field
• Significant senior leadership experience (10+ years) in product management, including running manager of managers structures
• Experience in deep tech, R&D intensive, or scientific product environments, bringing complex, research driven technology to market
• A track record of translating company strategy and customer insights into successful product strategy
• Experience translating technical innovation into scalable, commercially viable products
• Experience configuring a product portfolio for maximum customer value while optimizing commercial results
• Strong executive level communication skills, with the ability to align diverse stakeholders across functions and geographies
• Comfort working with ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-moving deep tech environment

Seen as an advantage

• Prior experience in quantum computing or an adjacent deep tech field
• Experience working with HPC centers, cloud providers, or sovereign cloud initiatives
• Prior experience with the important business models and their evolution over time in a computing industry

Why IQM?

• Full-stack quantum computing: From quantum hardware to software layers and beyond, we build across the full-stack.
• High-performance playground: We aim high, and we know sustainable performance only works when life outside work does too—hybrid setups, flexible hours.
• Never the smartest: You won’t always be the smartest person in the room. Neither will we. Expect to learn constantly - from each other and beyond with IQM’s Learning Hub, LinkedIn Learning, and a team-based L&D budget.
• Approachable leadership: Flat hierarchy, direct access. Feel free to approach any leaders. They're friendlier than they look!
• The sweet spot: Big enough to matter. Small enough to move fast. Growing between a startup and a corporation. We’re in the phase where top performers get noticed.
• Bigger than IQM: Our people build know-how for the entire quantum ecosystem. We publish papers, run hackathons, and help shape a market that's still being defined.

The future of computing won’t build itself. You might be one of the few who do.

• Meet our people and learn more about IQM on our stories page.
• Explore our scientific publications.

We'll start interviews and move forward with hiring as soon as we meet strong candidates. Please submit your application soon.

600M€+ Total Funding | 400+ Team Members | 30+ Quantum Computers Built | 300+ Patents Filed | 10 Location Globally

jobs.title: Product Quality Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.


We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in optics, systems, and scale. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a Product Quality Engineer to join our rapidly growing team.  This isn't just another role. This is a unique opportunity to own the technical vision for our products, work with a world-class multi-disciplinary team, and make a tangible impact from the ground up. The successful candidate will work closely with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and internal cross-functional development teams to meet product objectives and instill a culture of quality and continuous improvement.

What You'll Do:

 - Drive reliability execution for photonic components including Silicon Photonics ICs, lasers (DFB, CW lasers etc), and Optoelectronic SiPs used in high-speed optical networks.

 - Partner with R&D and design engineering to provide early reliability input during the product development lifecycle.

 - Define and execute qualification plans aligned with Telcordia/GR-468, JEDEC, and other relevant standards for telecom and datacom products.

 - Conduct accelerated life testing (ALT), failure analysis, degradation modeling, and root cause investigations to guide design and process improvement.

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including Photonics Design, Packaging, Manufacturing, Quality Engineering, Product Marketing and Supply Chain to ensure robust product development and transfer to production.

 - Lead supplier qualification activities and implement supplier quality metrics for critical photonics components.

 - Support supplier audits, assess factory capability, process controls, reliability models, and product roadmaps.

 - Support the infrastructure to perform incoming component validation

 - Develop and maintain Design for Reliability (DfR) methodologies, including predictive modeling and statistical analysis.

 - Prepare, present and document technical reviews, reliability reports, and risk assessments for internal and customer-facing engagements.

Key Qualifications:

 - M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, Materials Science, or related field, or equivalent experience in photonics reliability engineering with direct exposure to Silicon Photonics, laser technologies, and optical transceivers.

 - Strong background in photonics device physics, photonics packaging, and failure mechanisms.

 - Demonstrated success supporting NPI programs and product qualification from concept through volume production.

 - In-depth knowledge of relevant standards (GR-468, Telcordia, JEDEC, MIL-STD).

 - Proficiency with reliability modeling, statistical analysis (e.g., Weibull, Arrhenius), and tools such as JMP, Minitab, or similar.

 - Hands-on experience with reliability test systems (e.g., HTOL, HAST, T/H, TC), and FA tools (e.g., SEM, FIB, X-ray, spectroscopy).

 - Effective communicator with the ability to influence cross-functional and supplier teams.

 - Experience in a fast-paced, high-tech environment serving telecom/datacom markets.

Preferred Skills:

 - Experience in integrated photonics packaging and co-design (optical + electrical).

 - Familiarity with wafer-level reliability and optical wafer probing.

 - Prior experience on engagements with Tier-1 datacenter customers or hyperscalers.

Why Join Us?

This is more than a job. It's a chance to get in on the ground floor of a well-funded company set to disrupt a multi-billion dollar market. You will have the autonomy to make a massive impact, the resources to execute your vision, and a significant stake in the company you help build.

What we offer

 - Competitive salary commensurate with experience

 - Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance

 - Professional development opportunities and certification support

 - Access to cutting-edge technology and cloud platforms

 - Collaborative work environment with cross-functional teams

 - Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, identity, orientation, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

Working conditions

 - This position is onsite

 - May require quarterly off-site meetings or travel

 - Regular use of a computer and other office equipment is necessary

 - Interaction with team members and external contacts is a regular part of the job

 - May require occasional overtime and flexibility in work hours to accommodate the executive’s needs

jobs.title: Sales Team Coordinator | ON-SITE
jobs.description:
Bish Enterprises is seeking a proactive, organized, and customer-focused Sales Team Coordinator to support and coordinate the daily activities of our sales team.

This is a hands-on sales support, customer service, and people-coordination position. The employee will help organize priorities, monitor assignments, follow up with team members, coordinate communication, and make sure sales-related tasks continue moving forward.

The Sales Team Coordinator serves as a central point of communication between sales representatives, customers, management, and other departments.

Work Location

This is a full-time, on-site position located at:

508 S D Road

Giltner, Nebraska 68841

The employee is expected to work from the Bish Enterprises office during normal working hours.

This is not a remote or hybrid position.

Applicants must be able to reliably commute to the Giltner office.

A company laptop may be provided for business use. Receiving a company laptop does not make this a remote or hybrid position.

Travel Requirement

Some business travel is required.

Travel may include:

• Customer visits
• Trade shows
• Agricultural events
• Equipment demonstrations
• Training
• Sales meetings
• Dealer visits
• Other company-related activities

Travel may occasionally involve early mornings, evenings, weekends, or overnight stays.

The amount and location of travel may vary depending on customer needs, company events, sales activities, and the agricultural season.

The employee must be willing and able to travel when required.

Sales Team Coordination

The Sales Team Coordinator will help organize and coordinate the daily work of the sales team.

Responsibilities include:

• Helping communicate daily and weekly priorities to members of the sales team.
• Tracking sales-related assignments, deadlines, customer commitments, quotes, orders, and follow-up activities.
• Contacting team members for updates, missing information, and task completion.
• Reminding team members of deadlines, meetings, customer commitments, and required follow-ups.
• Making sure assigned tasks have a clear owner, deadline, and next step.
• Following up when work is incomplete, overdue, unclear, or missing.
• Helping organize and facilitate sales meetings.
• Preparing meeting agendas, notes, action items, assignments, and follow-up lists.
• Monitoring progress on action items discussed during meetings.
• Helping keep sales representatives aligned with company priorities and customer expectations.
• Identifying stalled opportunities, communication gaps, workload conflicts, or missing information.
• Escalating repeated delays, unresolved problems, or serious concerns to management.
• Helping maintain consistent use of the company’s CRM, calendars, sales procedures, and reporting systems.
• Assisting with onboarding and training coordination for new sales team members.
• Helping organize training materials, system access, schedules, meetings, and follow-up activities.

This role includes meaningful people coordination and day-to-day oversight of sales activities.

The employee may provide direction, follow-up, and accountability to members of the sales team. However, final authority regarding hiring, termination, compensation, formal discipline, and major personnel decisions remains with company management unless otherwise assigned.

Customer Service and Communication

The Sales Team Coordinator will help support customers throughout the sales process.

Responsibilities include:

• Answering customer phone calls, emails, and other inquiries in a friendly and professional manner.
• Gathering the information needed to understand the customer’s request.
• Directing technical, pricing, warranty, service, or product questions to the appropriate team member when necessary.
• Following up with customers regarding quotes, orders, availability, appointments, delivery information, and next steps.
• Providing customers with accurate information based on approved company materials and pricing.
• Communicating delays, changes, and updates clearly and promptly.
• Documenting customer commitments and making sure promised follow-ups are completed.
• Assisting with customer concerns by gathering information and coordinating with the appropriate department.
• Following customer issues through until they are resolved or transferred to the correct person.
• Representing Bish Enterprises professionally when communicating with customers, vendors, dealers, visitors, and industry contacts.

Quotes, Orders, and Sales Support

Responsibilities include:

• Preparing customer quotes, proposals, product information, and sales documents using company templates and approved pricing.
• Reviewing documents for accuracy and completeness before they are sent.
• Receiving customer orders and accurately entering the required information into company systems.
• Confirming customer contact information, products, pricing, delivery details, payment requirements, and other order information.
• Monitoring open quotes and orders to help prevent missed deadlines or incomplete tasks.
• Coordinating with production, parts, service, shipping, accounting, marketing, and other departments.
• Checking order status and identifying possible delays or missing information.
• Communicating order updates to the appropriate sales representative, customer, or manager.
• Scheduling customer calls, meetings, demonstrations, appointments, and follow-ups.
• Maintaining sales calendars and communicating scheduling changes.
• Assisting with preparation for trade shows, customer visits, sales meetings, and equipment demonstrations.

CRM, Reporting, and Administrative Support

Responsibilities include:

• Entering and maintaining customer, lead, quote, order, and follow-up information in the company’s systems.
• Keeping customer contact information, notes, deadlines, sales stages, and next steps complete and current.
• Preparing regular sales reports using information from the CRM, spreadsheets, and other company systems.
• Organizing information clearly for management and the sales team.
• Highlighting overdue follow-ups, open quotes, customer concerns, order issues, and other items requiring attention.
• Completing data entry, filing, document preparation, and record organization.
• Maintaining commonly used sales materials, templates, documents, and office supplies.
• Helping improve sales coordination procedures, tracking systems, and internal communication.

Independence and Accountability

The successful candidate must be able to work independently after receiving appropriate training.

The employee will be expected to:

• Keep track of assigned tasks and deadlines.
• Follow up without needing repeated reminders.
• Ask questions when instructions or information are unclear.
• Identify routine problems and take reasonable action to solve them.
• Find the correct person or resource when assistance is needed.
• Communicate delays, mistakes, or concerns promptly.
• Keep management informed about important customer, sales, or team issues.
• Address incomplete work professionally and respectfully.
• Balance being supportive with maintaining clear expectations.
• Work confidently with different personalities and communication styles.

This position may not be a good fit for someone who requires constant step-by-step direction for routine work or who is uncomfortable following up with coworkers about incomplete assignments.

Work Schedule

This is a full-time position that generally requires approximately 44 to 50 working hours per week.

The normal schedule is Monday through Friday.

Saturday, early-morning, evening, or additional hours may occasionally be required due to:

• Customer deadlines
• Company travel
• Trade shows or events
• Equipment demonstrations
• Agricultural seasonality
• Increased workload during busy periods

Some scheduling flexibility may be available with management approval.

Any schedule adjustment must still allow the employee to meet customer needs, attend required meetings, complete on-site responsibilities, coordinate the sales team, and fulfill travel requirements.

Because Bish Enterprises is a small and growing company, employees may occasionally be asked to assist with reasonable duties outside their normal task list.

People Coordination and Leadership Skills

• Ability to coordinate the daily work of the sales team members.
• Ability to clearly communicate assignments, priorities, deadlines, and expectations.
• Ability to follow up professionally when tasks or customer commitments are incomplete.
• Confidence asking team members for updates and required information.
• Ability to document responsibilities, deadlines, decisions, and next steps.
• Ability to lead or help facilitate sales meetings.
• Ability to identify when work is delayed, unclear, duplicated, or missing.
• Ability to address routine accountability concerns professionally.
• Ability to escalate serious or repeated issues to management.
• Ability to balance supporting team members with maintaining clear expectations.
• Ability to work with different personalities and communication styles.
• Ability to keep people organized and aligned without waiting for management to intervene in every situation.

Computer Skills

The employee must be comfortable using:

• Microsoft Outlook
• Microsoft Word
• Microsoft Excel
• Online calendars
• Customer relationship management systems
• Video meeting platforms
• Web-based business software
• Printers, scanners, telephones, and standard office equipment

The employee should be able to:

• Write clear and professional emails.
• Create, edit, save, and organize documents.
• Schedule meetings and manage calendar invitations.
• Enter data accurately.
• Sort and filter information in Excel.
• Use simple Excel formulas.
• Prepare small spreadsheets and basic reports.
• Create clear lists of assignments, owners, deadlines, and next steps.
• Learn new software with reasonable training.
• Perform basic office-equipment troubleshooting, such as reconnecting equipment or clearing a printer paper jam.

Preferred Qualifications

The following experience is preferred but may not be required:

• Previous experience coordinating employees, sales representatives, projects, schedules, or cross-functional teams.
• Previous experience in sales support.
• Customer-service experience.
• Administrative or office experience.
• Order-entry or order-processing experience.
• Experience preparing quotes or proposals.
• Experience using customer relationship management software.
• Experience leading meetings or tracking team assignments.
• Experience working with agricultural equipment, farming customers, machinery, manufacturing, parts, or service departments.
• Experience supporting trade shows, events, or customer demonstrations.
• Previous sales experience.

Applicants do not need to have held the exact title of Sales Team Coordinator.

Related experience in team coordination, customer service, office support, sales administration, order processing, project coordination, or account support may be considered.

Compensation

Wage is $40,000 base salary plus commission.

Expected yearly earnings are approximately $45,000–$70,000 during the first year. Actual earnings may vary based on performance, eligible sales, and the terms of the company’s commission plan.

Work Schedule

This is a full-time, on-site position located at Bish Enterprises in Giltner, Nebraska.

The normal work schedule is Monday through Friday, generally totaling approximately 44–50 hours per week.

Saturday, early-morning, evening, or additional hours may occasionally be required based on customer needs, company travel, trade shows, events, and agricultural seasonality.

Some scheduling flexibility may be available with management approval, provided that customer coverage, required meetings, on-site responsibilities, team coordination, and travel requirements are met.

This is not a remote or hybrid position.

Travel

Some business travel is required.

Travel may include customer visits, trade shows, agricultural events, equipment demonstrations, training, dealer visits, sales meetings, and other company-related activities.

Travel may occasionally include overnight stays, early mornings, evenings, or weekends.

The amount of travel may vary based on company needs and the agricultural season.

Benefits

Bish Enterprises offers a variety of benefits to eligible full-time employees. Benefits may include:

• Health insurance assistance
• Dental insurance
• Vision insurance
• Life insurance
• Paid time off
• Paid holidays
• Retirement plan options
• Employee discounts
• Professional development and training opportunities
• Company-provided equipment required for the position

Health Insurance

Bish Enterprises does not currently offer a traditional company-sponsored group health insurance plan.

Eligible employees may purchase individual health insurance through the federal Health Insurance Marketplace or another provider of their choice.

The company may provide a monthly health insurance contribution or reimbursement toward an eligible individual health insurance plan, subject to company policy and applicable requirements.

Employees are responsible for selecting, enrolling in, and maintaining their own individual health insurance coverage.

The availability and cost of Marketplace coverage may vary based on the employee’s household, location, income, selected plan, and eligibility for government subsidies.

Specific details regarding the company’s health insurance contribution or reimbursement will be explained during the hiring and enrollment process.

Benefit Eligibility

Some benefits are available only to employees who meet full-time status or other eligibility requirements.

Benefit eligibility, waiting periods, employee costs, company contributions, coverage terms, and plan availability are governed by the applicable company policies and benefit documents.

Benefits may be changed, replaced, or discontinued as permitted by law and company policy.

Other Information

A company laptop and other necessary equipment may be provided for business use.

Providing a company laptop does not make this a remote or hybrid position.

Because Bish Enterprises is a small and growing company, employees may occasionally be asked to perform reasonable duties outside their normal task list to support customers, coworkers, and changing business needs.

Regular and reliable attendance is an essential part of this position.

Employment with Bish Enterprises is at will. This means that either the employee or Bish Enterprises may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or advance notice, subject to applicable law.

Bish Enterprises is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to COO
jobs.description:
Bish Enterprises is seeking a highly organized, proactive, and dependable Executive Assistant to support our Chief Operating Officer (COO).

This role is much more than traditional administrative support. The Executive Assistant will help the COO manage priorities, organize information, coordinate communication, track commitments, and keep important projects and follow-ups moving across the company.

The right person will become a trusted administrative partner who can anticipate needs, manage multiple priorities, communicate professionally, and independently close open loops without requiring constant direction.

You should be comfortable working in an environment where priorities can change quickly, interruptions happen, and follow-through matters.

Key Responsibilities

Executive & Calendar Support

• Manage and maintain the COO's calendar, appointments, meetings, and scheduling priorities.
• Coordinate and confirm phone calls, Teams/Zoom meetings, appointments, and other commitments.
• Identify scheduling conflicts and help prioritize the COO's time.
• Make sure the COO has the documents, notes, links, background information, and other materials needed before meetings.
• Coordinate travel, accommodations, itineraries, events, and related logistics.
• Help keep the COO prepared for upcoming meetings, deadlines, commitments, and responsibilities.

Email, Communication & Follow-Up

• Help organize and maintain the COO's email inbox and communications.
• Track requests, commitments, deadlines, and follow-up items.
• Draft, format, proofread, and review emails, correspondence, reports, presentations, quotes, and other materials.
• Communicate professionally with employees, customers, vendors, industry partners, nonprofit organizations, and other external contacts.
• Make sure promised information and follow-ups are completed.
• Screen and appropriately direct incoming communications.
• Maintain professional relationship continuity on behalf of the COO.

Project & Team Coordination

• Follow up with team members across administration, sales, marketing, production, engineering, and other departments.
• Track project deliverables, deadlines, open questions, responsibilities, and next steps.
• Follow through on outstanding items until they are resolved.
• Help maintain accountability across projects and departments.
• Take clear meeting notes and turn discussions into organized action items.
• Keep project information, notes, and supporting documents organized.
• Update customer records, notes, CRM information, and project information when requested.

Administrative & Business Support

• Prepare presentations, reports, correspondence, meeting materials, and other documents.
• Organize and maintain electronic files and records.
• Conduct basic research and organize information for executive review.
• Assist with internal and external meetings, events, conferences, and speaking engagements.
• Provide administrative support for industry associations, nonprofit initiatives, and other organizational activities.
• Handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
• Assist with changing business and executive priorities as needed.

What Success Looks Like

A strong Executive Assistant at Bish does more than complete assigned tasks.

You should be someone who:

• Takes ownership of responsibilities and follows through.
• Notices when something is incomplete and works to resolve it.
• Keeps commitments, deadlines, and follow-ups from falling through the cracks.
• Understands what is urgent, what can wait, and when clarification is needed.
• Learns processes quickly and becomes increasingly independent.
• Takes useful notes and remembers recurring expectations.
• Communicates clearly and professionally with different personalities and departments.
• Is comfortable respectfully following up with coworkers and executives.
• Can manage interruptions and changing priorities without losing organization.
• Identifies practical solutions instead of simply reporting problems.
• Pays close attention to details while still understanding the larger priority.
• Can work independently without needing constant supervision.
• Knows when to take initiative and when to ask for direction.
• Is reliable, discreet, and trusted with sensitive information.

Required

• At least 2 years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Administrative Assistant, Office Administrator, or in a closely related support role.
• Strong organizational and time-management skills.
• Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
• Strong written and verbal English communication skills.
• Demonstrated reliability and follow-through.
• Ability to manage multiple responsibilities, deadlines, and changing priorities.
• Ability to work independently and take ownership of responsibilities.
• Strong judgment and discretion when handling sensitive or confidential information.
• Professional communication skills when interacting with executives, employees, customers, vendors, and external partners.
• Strong proficiency with Microsoft 365, including:OutlookWordExcelPowerPointTeams
• Strong computer skills and the ability to learn new systems quickly.
• Legally authorized to work in the United States.
• Able to work on-site at our Giltner, Nebraska location.

Preferred

• Experience directly supporting a COO, CEO, business owner, entrepreneur, or senior executive.
• Experience managing executive calendars and email inboxes.
• Experience coordinating projects across multiple departments.
• Experience with CRM systems.
• Experience with project-management tools such as Smartsheet, Trello, Asana, or similar platforms.
• Experience in sales support, marketing, public relations, business operations, or customer communication.
• Experience coordinating travel, conferences, events, or speaking engagements.
• Spanish language skills.
• Interest in agriculture, manufacturing, agricultural equipment, sustainability, or mission-driven organizations.

Agricultural experience is helpful but not required. We are more interested in finding someone who can learn quickly, understand the business, and become a reliable and increasingly independent partner to the COO.

Schedule

jobs.title: Operations & Warehouse Lead (Education Supply Chain, Part Time)
jobs.description:
About NORY

At NORY, we create extraordinary STEM learning experiences where children become curious problem-solvers, risk-taking entrepreneurs, and empathetic leaders. With 4,000+ campers annually across NYC and Boston, we are one of the region’s leading STEM camp providers. Families often describe NORY as the “Disney World of STEM education.” That level of quality depends on thoughtful systems, strong execution, and excellent operations behind the scenes.

We are looking for a full-time Operations & Warehouse Lead to help lead that work.

Learn more:

 - Instagram: bit.ly/noryi http://bit.ly/noryi

 - LinkedIn: bit.ly/norylink http://bit.ly/norylink

 - Summer Camp Video: bit.ly/noryvideo1 http://bit.ly/noryvideo1

Why This Role Is Exciting

This is not a passive warehouse role or a narrow logistics job. It is a high-ownership role at the center of a growing company.

You will:

 - Take ownership of a mission-critical part of the business

 - Build systems that improve efficiency and scale across multiple sites

 - Lead and develop a team

 - Work closely with leadership

 - See the direct impact of your work on programs serving thousands of families

 - Grow in a fast-moving organization where strong ideas and strong execution are truly valued

If you like solving problems, building better processes, and being the person who makes things happen, this role will be a strong fit.

What You’ll Do

Warehouse & Inventory Management

 - Oversee daily warehouse operations, including organization, inventory tracking, and material flow

 - Build and maintain strong inventory systems so materials are always stocked, accurate, and easy to access

 - Keep the workspace clean, safe, and highly functional

Materials Production & Preparation

 - Lead preparation of enrichment materials across arts, woodworking, and engineering programs

 - Ensure a high bar for accuracy, efficiency, and quality

Logistics & Supply Chain

 - Own the full logistics cycle: ordering, preparation, packing, transportation, and campsite setup

 - Coordinate deliveries and movement of materials across NYC locations

Team Leadership & Management

 - Manage and support the maker and warehouse team

 - Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and follow-through

Operations & Process Improvement

 - Create and refine systems, workflows, and protocols

 - Identify inefficiencies and implement scalable improvements

Cross-Functional Coordination

 - Ensure materials and logistics are aligned with program goals and timelines

 - Design practical, efficient warehouse organization that supports speed and scale

Who You Are

You may be a strong fit if you are:

 - Highly organized and detail-oriented

 - Naturally proactive and dependable

 - Comfortable owning both strategy and execution

 - A strong problem-solver who likes improving systems

 - Clear and professional in how you communicate

 - Comfortable leading people while also staying close to the work

 - Motivated by impact, responsibility, and growth

Requirements

 - Ability to lift 20+ lbs

 - Ability to stand, walk, bend, and perform physical tasks for extended periods

 - Comfort navigating NYC for deliveries and logistics coordination

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means:

 - Materials are prepared accurately and on time

 - The warehouse runs smoothly and stays organized

 - Logistics are proactive rather than reactive

 - The maker team is supported and productive

 - Systems improve over time instead of becoming more complicated

 - Camp sites and programs consistently have what they need to succeed

Join Our Vision:

We're searching for an Operations & Warehouse Lead who is not just skilled and passionate but also aligns deeply with our core values. At NORY, our 'Ways of Being' guide everything we do:

 - We are purposeful in our actions, always asking "why" to cultivate inner motivation.

 - We ask "how to make it work" before wondering "if it will be possible."

 - Our decisions are grounded in data and logic.

 - We are accountable and disciplined.

 - We actively seek feedback, embracing different perspectives and effective methods that contribute to our growth.

 - We avoid superficial solutions, opting instead to thoroughly analyze problems to create sustainable, scalable responses.

 - We are unifiers, fostering a loving and caring team environment that deeply values empathy and compassion.

These aren't just words; they're the essence of our DNA. If these values speak to you, see how you align with our complete 'Ways of Being' at www.nory.co/value http://www.nory.co/value

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary: $20 - $25 per hour (based on experience)

 - 401(k)

How to Apply

If you have a compelling reason to work with us, we’d love to hear from you. Please send a personalized email to sofia@nory.co with your resume and a few lines about what excites you about this role.

NORY – Operations & Warehouse Lead Application - Part Time

jobs.title: Failure Analysis Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.



POSITION OVERVIEW

As a Failure Analysis Engineer at Lumilens, you will play a critical role in ensuring the reliability and performance of our advanced optical transceiver products. You’ll lead the investigation of optical, electrical, and mechanical failures either from field deployments or production testing, using schematics, test equipment, and fault isolation techniques to identify root causes and drive corrective actions. Partnering closely with R&D, supplier quality, and production teams, you’ll document findings, assess field risks, and communicate insights that directly influence product design and manufacturing improvements. 



This role also involves developing new test infrastructure, writing automation scripts for customer switches, and occasionally engaging directly with customers on technical inquiries. It’s a highly collaborative, hands-on position at the intersection of engineering, quality, and innovation.  This role is ideal for someone passionate about problem solving and driving continuous improvement in cutting edge optical technologies.



DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Responsible for optical, mechanical and electrical analysis/troubleshooting of optical transceivers returned from field deployment or internal testing.

 - Troubleshoot failures using schematics, test equipment, switches, fault isolation techniques, and Design of Experiments

 - Work with cross-functional teams, including supplier quality engineers, to determine the root cause(s) and appropriate improvement/corrective actions

 - Thorough documentation of all test and failure analysis results, including photographs, test data, and repair work

 - Interface with production databases to extract original shipment information, test data, and traceability information.

 - Assess field risk based on understanding of failure modes and field data utilizing available reliability tools

 - Analyze and present periodic and timely updates on failure analysis progress and reliability estimates to R&D, corporate teams, and customers

 - Engage in discussion with customers and respond to direct technical inquiries

 - Bring-up new internal and external test infrastructure to validate failure signatures observed in customer environments

 - Develop test scripts to operate and report data from customer switches

 - Experience in datacenter architecture is a plus
   

SKILLS/EXPERIENCE

 - Minimum 5 yr. experience of related experience.  Experiences in transceiver module tests at 400G, 800G, 1.6T, etc., are preferred.

 - BS/MS in physics, electrical/Mechanical engineering or other relevant field or equivalent experience

 - Extensive knowledge of and experience working with analog and digital circuits

 - Familiar with MSA and customer standards/requirements

 - Familiar with basic failure analysis techniques/methodologies

 - Strong device physics background

 - Fundamental understanding of OSA assembly and its periphery circuits

 - Knowledge of OSA assemblies, PCBA, and module manufacturing processes is an added advantage

 - Working knowledge of device characterization and its techniques

 - Strong data analysis skills

 - Excellent verbal and written communication skills



All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by local law, regulation, or ordinance.

jobs.title: Technical Writer
jobs.description:
Radar Reinvented.

Echodyne offers the world’s first compact solid-state true beam-steering radar for a wide range of industries and applications. Our high-performance radars work in all weather and are designed for autonomous vehicles, uncrewed aircraft & drones, and security of borders, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. The company combines the patented technology of metamaterials with powerful software to create a radar sensor with unprecedented performance at commercial price points. Echodyne offers its radars to companies working in Automotive, Transportation, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Border Security, Smart Cities, Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Airspace Management including Urban Air Mobility (UTM).

Echodyne is seeking a Technical Writer to join our fast-growing team.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Own the planning, development, validation, publication, localization, and lifecycle maintenance of documentation for assigned radar hardware products.

• Create user guides, quick-start guides, installation and configuration procedures, system-integration guides, operation and troubleshooting content, and other customer-facing technical materials with a focus on hardware components and assemblies.

• Partner with systems, hardware, software, test/QA, product, support, program management, manufacturing or operations, and training stakeholders throughout the product lifecycle.

• Author and maintain modular content using DITA XML or other approved structured-authoring formats, applying topic-based writing, metadata, conditional content, and reuse strategies.

• Contribute through Git-based docs-as-code workflows, including branches, commits, pull requests, peer review, issue tracking, change traceability, and automated build or publishing processes.

• Manage multiple documentation initiatives independently, communicate risks early, and adapt plans as product priorities change.

REQUIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE

• Six or more years of professional technical-writing experience, including substantial experience documenting complex hardware-and-software products or systems.

• A portfolio or work samples demonstrating clear, task-oriented documentation for technical products; installation, operation, maintenance, integration, or troubleshooting samples are especially relevant.

• Demonstrated ability to learn through hands-on product use and to validate documentation against hardware, software, or realistic test environments.

• Experience with DITA XML or another topic-based structured-authoring methodology, including content reuse, metadata, conditional publishing, and multi-format output.

• Hands-on experience with docs-as-code workflows and Git, including repositories, branches, commits, pull requests or merge requests, peer review, and issue tracking.

• Ability to interpret complex engineering source material and translate it into content that technical and less-technical audiences can understand and act on.

• Strong project-management skills, attention to detail, and the ability to independently prioritize multiple documentation deliverables in a changing environment.

• Bachelor's degree in technical communication, engineering, computer science, English, communications, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

DESIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE
(Looking for one or more as a complement to the core skills)

• Experience documenting radar, aerospace, defense, government, industrial, embedded, electronic, or other mission-critical systems.

• Proficiency with Oxygen XML Editor and experience with a component content management system (CCMS), DITA Open Toolkit, XSLT, CSS, or related publishing technologies.

• Familiarity with Agile product development, engineering change control, release management, and documentation traceability.

• Experience creating technical diagrams, annotated product images, or other visual explanations from engineering source material.

This is an exempt role.

• Develop role-based curricula and learning paths for customers, including onboarding, product releases, and continuing education.

• Evaluate learning effectiveness using learner feedback, assessment results, field-readiness indicators, and stakeholder input.

• Recommend improvements based on performance data, product changes, customer needs, and lessons learned in the field.

• Proficiency with an e-learning authoring platform such as Articulate 360, Adobe Captivate, or an equivalent tool.

• Experience creating meaningful assessments, hands-on exercises, and scenario-based learning.
