jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Member Experience
jobs.description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job Overview:

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to own a significant piece of Omada's Member-facing surface. You own what gets built, in what order, and how the people building it grow.

A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships. At this level you own more than one, which means the hardest calls you make are the ones about where capacity goes when two good things want it at the same time.

You stay technical. You are in the codebase and in the same agent workflows your builders use, close enough to review architecture, catch a weak design, and be useful in an incident. Where you manage directly, you ship production work off the critical path. Where you manage through someone else, that person's growth is your work product.

You partner with Product Strategists who spend their time in front of members, coaches, and stakeholders, and who prototype to test ideas quickly. They own what gets built and why. You own whether it can be delivered, at what cost, and by when, and you are senior enough that your answer shapes the roadmap rather than just responding to it.

About you:

You are comfortable being accountable for what your squads ship. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agent workflows as your squads, so you feel the friction your people feel first-hand.

You have a point of view on where AI-assisted development helps and where it creates rework, and it comes from changing how a real team works, not from reading about it. You have done the engineering manager job well enough that you can teach it. Whether or not you have carried the title of manager-of-managers, you have grown someone into leading, and you know the difference between doing the work for them and raising their ceiling.

Your first team is your peer group, not your reports. When something is slowing down the engineering org and it is nobody's job, you have a track record of picking it up, getting the right people in the room, and finishing it.

What you'll be doing:

• Own delivery across your squads. Sprint shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation. Make the calls, write them down, and be accountable for them. When two squads want the same thing at the same time, you are the one who decides.

• Own cycle time. Yours to improve, not at the expense of quality, and yours to explain when it changes, including why one of your squads is slower than the other.

• Stay technical. On squads you manage directly, you ship production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same agent workflows your builders use. On squads that run through a manager, you stay close enough to review architecture, catch a weak design, and be useful in an incident. Either way, you can teach someone to navigate the system, not just navigate it yourself.

• Partner with your Product Strategist. They own what the squad builds; you hold the line between their scope and yours so the squad never has two people answering the same question differently.

• Grow a manager. If an EM reports to you, their growth is your work product. Their squad's health is the evidence.

• Plan the team you need next year, not just this quarter. Headcount, skill mix, and the onboarding path that gets a new builder productive in an agent-heavy codebase in weeks rather than months.

• Set the AI standard past your own boundary. Write down what good looks like, teach it, and measure whether it stuck. Other squads should be able to use what you built without you in the room.

• Take on the problem that is nobody's. You will find things that slow down engineering broadly. Some of them you should pick up, organize, and close out with your peers.

What you need for this role:

• 8+ years in software engineering, including 4+ years managing engineers directly.

• Experience developing another leader: a manager who reported to you, or an engineer you grew into a tech lead or EM role with real accountability attached. Tell us where they are now.

• A track record shipping mission-critical software to production, and living with it afterwards. We all make mistakes; what sets you apart is that you own yours and turn them into something better.

• Experience owning prioritization and estimation for a team, including saying no, not now, and explaining why.

• Experience giving direct developmental feedback, and at least one case where you managed someone through underperformance with real support attached.

• Currently shipping, or recently shipping, production code in at least one layer of our stack (backend (Ruby, Python, ...), web frontends (React), iOS, or Android,) with enough range to follow the conversation in the others and review architecture decisions critically.

• Comfort with an expert-generalist team model, where a backend-heavy builder ships in the mobile app and a mobile-heavy one ships in the backend. You understand how transformative this model is, and you should be able to name the risks and opportunities it brings.

• Hands-on experience directing AI agents through real world production changes, and a considered view on where they help and where they produce work someone else has to redo.

• Understanding of CI/CD, logging, monitoring, and telemetry, at the level where you can tell whether your squad's operational story checks out or falls short.

• Excellent written communication. Much of this job is writing things down clearly once so they do not have to be argued four times.

Technologies we use:

Ruby on Rails, Python (Flask, FastAPI), React, native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI), native Android (Kotlin), PostgreSQL, GraphQL, AWS (RDS, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, GitLab, Datadog, PagerDuty.

Benefits:

• Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus

• Equity grants

• Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP)

• Remote first work from home culture

• Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones

• Generous parental leave

• Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)

• 401k retirement savings plan

• Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)

• Mental Health Support Solutions

• ...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!

• Cultivate Trust. We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.

• Seek Context. We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.

• Act Boldly. We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.

• Deliver Results. We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.

• Succeed Together. We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.

• Remember Why We’re Here. We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health: Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

Omada is thrilled to share that we’ve been certified as a Great Place to Work! Please click here for more information.

We carefully hire the best talent we can find, which means actively seeking diversity of beliefs, backgrounds, education, and ways of thinking. We strive to build an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated and leveraged to inform better design and business decisions. Omada is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, legally protected medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws.

jobs.title: Global Supply Manager, Satellites (Starmind)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER, SATELLITES (STARMIND)

The SpaceX Supply Chain Department is a critical player in our operations. To capitalize on our technical and market success, our team will execute large-scale projects that will define the bottom line for the company. Functions within the department include procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics, and inventory. As a Global Supply Manager in Bastrop, you will support the commodities used to manufacture Starmind satellites at one of the most vertically integrated manufacturing facilities in existence, enabling launch of the constellation into orbit.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Develop and manage the supply base to support sourcing for the technology to build orbital data-center satellites

• Provide weekly team status reporting, escalating to leadership when necessary

• Train and mentor others, working to ensure the team is continuously improving

• Work directly with key suppliers to develop and implement sourcing and cost-management strategies that support existing platforms and new product development

• Work directly with key internal stakeholders to develop and implement sourcing and cost-management strategies that support capital purchases and production consumables

• Understand the technical aspects of production equipment to identify opportunities for cost, space, and process optimization; use data analytics to identify and prioritize process-related opportunities

• Negotiate to maximize value, cost savings, and delivery priority for SpaceX while lowering risk and aligning costs with program budgets

• Build and own overall project budgets, compile funding requests, and generate capitalization plans based on project timeline, focusing on total cost of ownership (TCO) of the categories managed

• Conduct research, performance benchmarking, and market analysis for assigned categories

• Communicate overall equipment status to the leadership team, including schedules, risks, and mitigation actions, responding quickly to changes in overall goals, schedule, and architecture

• Create sourcing strategies to reduce risk, enable continuous cost reduction, and align with company strategy on payment terms, cash targets, on-time delivery, and cost savings

• Build genuine relationships internally and externally and drive cross-functional teams to achieve consensus

• Present value propositions to SpaceX executives, including those related to contract awards, cost reviews, cost reduction strategies, and critical supply issues

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:

• Engineering

• Purchasing

• Contract negotiation

• Material or production planning

• Operations or supply chain management

• Material cost control

• Master production scheduling

• Capital equipment sourcing

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 8+ years of experience directly negotiating contracts and sourcing global suppliers

• 8+ years of experience with sourcing from a global supply base, and familiarity interfacing in-person with suppliers around the world

jobs.title: Performance Creative Manager
jobs.description:
The Company
VeSync is a portfolio company with brands that cover different categories of health & wellness products. We wouldn't be surprised if you have one of our Levoit air purifiers in your living room or a COSORI air fryer whipping up healthy and delicious meals for you every night.
We're a young and energetic company, we've had tremendous success, and we are constantly growing our team. As we garner more industry attention — just check out our accomplishments and awards by CES Innovation, iF Design, IGA, and Red Dot — we also need driven and talented people to join our team.
That brings us to you, and what you'll be joining. Our teams are smart and diligent and take ownership of their work — they're confident in their work but know how to collaborate with open ears and a spirit of learning. If you're down-to-earth, approachable, and easy to strike up a conversation with, this may be a great fit for you.
Check out our other brands: levoit.com | cosori.com | etekcity.com
The Opportunity
A new ecosystem at the intersection of wellness and technology, with a connected product, hardware and software, built to help people take an active role in their own health rather than simply measure it. The Creative Strategist owns the concepts behind the advertising that brings people to it.
Your job is to build the pipeline: the angles, the hooks, and the concepts that fill our paid channels, and the system that keeps producing them week after week. The platforms now match ads to people on the creative itself rather than on who we target, so the work is genuinely different concepts at volume, not variations of the same one. We are pre-launch, and the brand, the positioning, and the claims we can make are all still being built. You'll start from a CAC target, a hypothesis, and a testing roadmap rather than from an account with history. It's a hands-on role.
Key Responsibilities
Concept & Pipeline
Own the Concept Pipeline: Generate genuinely distinct concepts, hooks, and angles at the volume and variety the platforms reward. Near-identical ads get treated as one, so diversity is the job, not output alone.
Write the Briefs: Customer insight, hook, format, shot list, testing variable, and the hypothesis behind each one. Enough direction that production isn't guessing.
Build the System: Brief templates, concept taxonomy, naming and tagging conventions, and the intake process that keeps a weekly cadence moving. Most of this gets built before the first dollar is spent.
Production & Partners
Keep the Pipeline Fed: Work with internal graphics and video, agency partners, and creators to get concepts made. Sequence production so the calendar stays ahead of fatigue.
Brief the Creators: Partner with Creator Partnerships on angles and creator briefs, and confirm paid usage rights are covered before the work gets made.
Work Inside the Claims Line: Claim-bearing creative goes through medical, regulatory, and legal review. Build a library of approved hooks and language so the pipeline keeps moving rather than queuing.
Testing & Reuse
Read the Numbers: Hook rate, hold rate, CTR, CVR, CPA. Find the winners, diagnose the losers, kill fast, and iterate on what works.
Stay Ahead of Fatigue: Concepts decay quickly. Keep the refresh cadence ahead of the decline rather than reacting to it.
Make Assets Work Twice: Carry winning hooks and assets into lifecycle, email, on-site, and organic social. You supply the raw material, those owners decide what fits their channel.
Qualifications
We are seeking a performance-minded creative who can build a concept pipeline from nothing and is comfortable being measured on what it produces.
Education: Bachelor's degree required.
Experience: 4+ years in performance creative, direct response, or paid social for consumer (B2C) brands, with hands-on direct-to-consumer (DTC) experience. Titles vary in this space. What matters is that you have run the loop: research, hypothesis, brief, production, test, iterate.
Platform Fluency: Deep working knowledge of how creative performs on Meta and why. This starts on Meta and expands across channels, so full-channel experience is a plus.
Angles, Not Variations: Can show concepts you personally wrote, the brief behind each, and what the numbers did. Knows the difference between a new angle and a new edit.
Comfortable with Ambiguity: Can build while the brand, the positioning, and the claims framework are still being settled. Starts from a CAC target and a hypothesis rather than waiting for an account with history.
Claims & Regulatory Fluency: Experience in health, wellness, medical device, supplements, or a similarly regulated space. Knows how to write a strong hook that survives review.
Analytical: Reads creative performance honestly and uses it to decide what gets made next. Comfortable killing their own ideas.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partners closely with media buying, creator partnerships, brand and creative, product, and lifecycle.
Nice to Have: Light production ability. Low or mid-fidelity mockups, simple graphics, or rough cuts that get a concept tested faster. Comfort on camera for native short-form is a bonus. This is not the job, it is speed.
 
Location: Tustin, CA
Starting Salary: 150K
Perks and Benefits
100% covered Medical/Dental/Vision insurances for employee AND spouse + dependents!
401K with 4% employer match (eligible after 90 days of employment) and immediate 100% vesting
Generous PTO policy + paid holidays
Life Insurance

Accident Insurance

jobs.title: Enterprise Systems Architect
jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

Position Summary

We are seeking an Enterprise Systems Architect to define and lead the technology architecture supporting our cloud infrastructure, endpoint management, and manufacturing applications. This role will oversee Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Intune, and manufacturing platforms such as Manufacturo, DELMIA Apriso, Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE, or similar.

The Enterprise Architect will partner with IT, cybersecurity, engineering, and manufacturing teams to design secure, reliable, and scalable solutions that connect enterprise systems with plant operations. This is a hands-on architecture role responsible for technology strategy, design standards, integration, and technical oversight of implementation on Voyager’s classified and non-classified systems.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain the enterprise architecture roadmap for Azure, endpoint management, and manufacturing applications.

• Define Azure architecture standards for networking, identity, security, governance, resilience, monitoring, and cost management.

• Establish Microsoft Intune architecture and standards for device enrollment, configuration, application deployment, compliance, patching, and endpoint security.

• Guide the architecture, implementation, integration, and modernization of Manufacturo, Apriso, 3DEXPERIENCE, and related manufacturing and engineering systems.

• Design integrations among manufacturing execution systems (MES), product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), quality systems, and enterprise data platforms.

• Partner with plant operations and operational technology (OT) teams to address connectivity, security, production availability, and change management requirements.

• Define identity and access patterns using Microsoft Entra ID, role-based access control, single sign-on, and Conditional Access.

• Establish application lifecycle, environment, disaster recovery, and business continuity requirements aligned with operational needs.

• Evaluate technology and vendor proposals for architectural fit, integration complexity, supportability, and total cost of ownership.

• Maintain architecture diagrams, reference designs, integration standards, and technical decision records.

• Lead architecture reviews and provide technical direction to internal teams, implementation partners, and managed service providers.

• Translate business requirements into actionable solution designs and communicate recommendations to technical teams and business leadership.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Eight or more years of progressive experience in enterprise IT, infrastructure, or application architecture, including at least three years in an architecture leadership role.

• Demonstrated experience designing and governing Microsoft Azure environments, including identity, networking, security, monitoring, and hybrid connectivity.

• Strong experience with Microsoft Intune, Windows endpoint management, application deployment, device compliance, and Microsoft Entra ID.

• Experience architecting or integrating manufacturing or engineering applications.

• Understanding of manufacturing processes and the role of MES, PLM, ERP, traceability, and quality management systems.

• Experience designing integrations using APIs, middleware, messaging, and enterprise data services.

• Ability to design for security, availability, scalability, and recovery while accounting for production constraints.

• Experience leading technical projects and coordinating across business stakeholders, IT teams, and external vendors.

• Strong documentation, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting multiple manufacturing facilities or enterprise-wide manufacturing transformation initiatives.

• Experience with two or more manufacturing platforms such as 3D Experience, Apriso, Manufacturo, CQ, or others.

• Familiarity with IT/OT segmentation, shop-floor connectivity, and industrial cybersecurity practices.

• Experience supporting digital thread initiatives that connect product design, manufacturing execution, and product lifecycle data.

• Familiarity with infrastructure as code, automated deployments, and architecture governance frameworks such as NIST 800-171, CMMS, DoD STIGs, Secure Cloud Services (SACA, SCCA).

• Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated manufacturing environments.

The good faith base salary range for this role is $165,000–$195,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

• Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance

• Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources

• The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission-driven environment

jobs.title: Senior Staff Network Engineer, Deployment
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Crusoe Cloud is seeking a Senior Staff Network Deployment Engineer to serve as the technical owner of how we deploy network infrastructure across our global fleet. As we rapidly scale our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure, you will define the deployment strategy, set the standards, and architect the automation platform that brings new data centers and edge sites online — at a pace and scale few companies have ever attempted.

This is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and Infrastructure Strategy. You will partner with Network Architecture to shape designs for deployability, mentor a team of Staff and Senior engineers executing your vision, and represent the deployment org in cross-functional planning with Supply Chain, Data Center Ops, and Site Reliability leadership. You're not refining a runbook — you're authoring the playbook that defines how the world's most innovative AI cloud comes online.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON

 - Own Global Deployment Strategy: Define the multi-quarter technical roadmap for how Crusoe deploys network infrastructure across new and existing data centers, edge sites, and backbone interconnects.

 - Set the Standards: Author and ratify internal RFCs and technical standards for physical and logical network deployment — cabling, optics, fabric provisioning, validation, and handoff — that the broader engineering org executes against.

 - Influence Architecture for Deployability: Partner closely with Network Architecture to shape designs that scale operationally; serve as the senior voice ensuring what gets designed can actually be built and validated at hyperscale pace.

 - Architect the Deployment Automation Platform: Set the technical direction for Crusoe's ZTP, IaC, and validation tooling stack. Drive the strategy for Python-, Ansible-, and CI/CD-based systems that stage and validate hundreds of devices simultaneously.

 - Define the Validation Framework: Establish the burn-in, site acceptance testing (SAT), and commissioning criteria used across the fleet to ensure zero-defect handovers to Operations.

 - Lead Vendor and Partner Strategy: Establish standards, SLAs, and qualification programs for structured cabling vendors, remote hands partners, and data center providers globally. Influence hardware vendor roadmaps (Arista, Juniper, NVIDIA/Mellanox) based on Crusoe's operational needs.

 - Drive Capacity and Asset Strategy: Partner with Supply Chain and Infrastructure leadership on capacity planning, hardware lifecycle, and the turn-up cadence for new backbone capacity and edge interconnects.

 - Mentor and Multiply: Provide technical guidance to Staff and Senior network deployment engineers. Lead design reviews, post-incident reviews, and drive systemic improvements to deployment quality across the org.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 12+ years of network engineering experience with a heavy focus on large-scale data center deployments and infrastructure programs, including significant time in hyperscale, large cloud, or ISP environments.

 - Python

 - Demonstrated Technical Leadership: Proven track record of authoring standards, mentoring engineers, and driving multi-quarter technical initiatives that span teams. You've operated as a senior technical voice in an organization where decisions you've made are still in production.

 - Hyperscale Operational Experience: Comfort operating at scale — 10K+ network devices, multi-region fabric deployments, and the realities of building when the supply chain, the timeline, and the physics are all working against you.

 - Mastery of Physical Layer Standards: Deep expertise in structured cabling (SMF/MMF, MPO/MTP), optical transceivers (400G/800G and roadmap to 1.6T), and data center power/cooling for HPC workloads.

 - Routing and Switching Fluency: Expert hands-on experience with Arista (EOS), Juniper (Junos), and NVIDIA/Mellanox platforms in leaf-spine architectures. You can go as deep as the problem demands.

 - Protocol Proficiency: Strong working knowledge of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, and LLDP as they relate to large-scale fabric provisioning and validation.

 - Automation Architect: Track record of designing and shipping deployment automation systems used by a broader engineering team — not just scripts you wrote, but platforms others build on. Strong Python and Ansible; familiarity with modern IaC and CI/CD patterns.

 - Program Leadership: Proven ability to lead multiple complex, concurrent deployment programs across time zones and physical locations, with executive-level communication and risk management.

 - Diagnostic Depth: Able to diagnose complex physical layer and link-layer issues using OTDRs, light meters, and packet captures — and able to teach others to do the same.

 - Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience in hyperscale or ISP environments.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $225,000 - $275,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering physician-led, evidence-based care for obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions. Obesity affects more than 40% of U.S. adults, and as GLP-1 medications reshape the field, Obesity and Cardiometabolic Medicine is in a period of rapid growth and opportunity. Form Health is at the forefront of that shift, building a clinical model that combines rigorous, personalized medical care with the technology to make it accessible at scale.

Every Form Health patient works closely with a dedicated multidisciplinary Care Team, including board-certified physicians (many ABOM-certified, and endocrinologists), advanced practice providers, and Registered Dietitians who together deliver comprehensive, one-on-one treatment that includes nutrition, behavioral health, physical activity, and FDA-approved medication, if appropriate. Through our mobile app, patients engage in regular video visits along with text messaging, photo journaling, and personalized educational content. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.

Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed, mission-driven company partnering with leading employers and health plans to expand access to high-quality, guideline-based obesity and cardiometabolic care nationwide. We're deeply invested in our core value of putting patients first, and equally committed to building a culture where every employee is valued and we learn and grow together.

About the Role:

The Senior Program Manager, Product is a critical, highly independent role at the center of Form Health's Product organization. You'll be the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Clinical, and go-to-market teams — and the person responsible for making sure our Product org operates as a best-in-class, AI-forward, product development team.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's. You'll define the Product Operations roadmap from the ground up, bring in and champion cutting-edge tools and methodologies (including AI-assisted planning, development, and research workflows), and continuously raise the bar on how the team plans, ships, and learns. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy — setting priorities, making judgment calls, and driving initiatives to completion with minimal oversight — while staying closely aligned with Product, Engineering, and executive stakeholders.

What You Will Do:

• Own the Product Operations roadmap: Independently define the vision, priorities, and success metrics for how the Product org plans, builds, ships, and learns — identifying gaps and driving initiatives from idea to adoption.

• Drive end-to-end program management: Own execution roadmaps for key cross-functional initiatives — from new clinical program features to platform investments — ensuring timely, high-quality delivery from concept to launch.

• Orchestrate cross-functional alignment: Serve as the connective tissue between Product, Engineering, Design, Clinical Operations, Marketing, and Customer Success — facilitating the rituals, decisions, and communication that keep every team moving in the same direction.

• Champion AI-forward tools and methodologies: Evaluate, pilot, and roll out modern product development tooling — AI-assisted planning, coding, research, and automation — to help the team plan and ship faster. Treat AI as core infrastructure for how the team works, not a side project.

• Build and evolve the product operating model: Design and continuously improve how the team runs, including intake and triage processes, roadmap and sprint rituals, documentation standards, and tooling that scale with the company.

• Turn data and feedback into decisions: Synthesize product usage data, clinical and operational metrics, and patient/customer feedback into clear, actionable recommendations that inform roadmap and prioritization.

• Provide executive visibility: Develop and deliver program health readouts and roadmap updates to leadership, with data-driven insights, risks, and recommendations.

• Proactively manage risk and dependencies: Identify, assess, and mitigate issues that could impact timelines or quality across teams, escalating and resolving blockers before they become critical.

• Interface directly with stakeholders: Act as a trusted partner and clear point of contact for Product-related questions from Clinical, Commercial, Ops, and executive leadership.

About You:

• 5+ years of progressive experience in program/project management, product operations, or a related discipline within a fast-paced software or digital health environment.

• A demonstrated track record of operating highly independently — you've built a roadmap, process, or operating model from scratch, not just executed against someone else's plan.

• Fluency with modern product development tools and genuine enthusiasm for AI-forward workflows (e.g., AI-assisted planning, coding, and research tools, alongside Linear, Figma, etc.).

• Deep understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and Agile methodologies, with the judgment to adapt them to what a team actually needs rather than applying them rigidly.

• Strong analytical skills — comfortable pulling and interpreting product, engineering, and operational data to inform decisions.

• Outstanding cross-functional communication and influence — able to distill ambiguous, complex problems into clear plans and align stakeholders, from ICs to executives, without relying on direct authority.

• Experience in digital health, healthcare operations, or another regulated/clinical environment is a strong plus.

• Bachelor's degree in a technical, business, or related field preferred; PMP, PgMP, or similar certification a plus.

More about Form Health’s benefits:

• Competitive salary and equity in a high growth start-up

• Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)

• 401k program

• Flexible work schedules and paid time off

• Paid parental leave

Form Health’s commitment to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment:

Form Health is committed to creating a culture and environment that celebrates diversity and inclusion, while fostering safety and belonging. This extends from our remote patient care to our corporate offices and everywhere in between. We are looking for team members who want to help us further our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) efforts and who share our attitudes for creating an inclusive, safe, and positive work environment.

Base Annual Salary

$140,000—$165,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (West Coast USA)
jobs.description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

Senior Software Engineer

Location: Remote (West Coast USA)

Company: MISUMI Americas

PLEASE NOTE:  Final-round interviews will be conducted in person in either Oakland, California, or Portland, Oregon.

Build the Future of Manufacturing

Manufacturing is a $13 trillion industry, and most of it is still held together by spreadsheets, phone calls, and fax machines. MISUMI Americas is rewriting that.

We've been building a cloud-based, AI-powered digital manufacturing platform that takes companies from prototype to production faster than the industry thought possible. Our platform pairs intelligent software with a global network of vetted manufacturing partners, powering innovation across electric vehicles, robotics, and next-generation consumer products.

We're scaling fast, and we're looking for engineers who'd rather untangle hard, real-world problems than push pixels on a toy app.

You'll join the team that owns costing, pricing, lead time, and DFM (design for manufacturability) for our instant quoting platform.  When a customer uploads a part, our systems decide what it costs, when it ships, and whether it can be made.  Accuracy matters; our output directly drives revenue and customer trust.

We build with AI agents as a core part of how we work.  We're looking for strong engineers who use agents to plan, implement, and test faster, and who have the judgment to know when the output is wrong.

What You'll Do

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you'll help build and scale the systems running our global manufacturing ecosystem:

• Design and develop highly available, scalable backend services in AWS

• Build and maintain event-driven, asynchronous systems using Node.js

• Create robust APIs (REST / GraphQL) powering customer-facing and internal tools

• Use AI coding agents to take features from design through implementation and testing, while owning the correctness of every change

• Write specs, tests, and repo context that make agent-driven development reliable in a large, established codebase

• Partner closely with product, frontend, and infrastructure teams to ship features that actually move the business

• Contribute to technical design discussions and drive best practices across the team

• Help shape how the team works with AI: sharing patterns, tooling, and lessons learned

• Debug production issues and improve system reliability

• Continuously improve code quality through testing, observability, and documentation

What You Bring

• 5 + years of backend engineering experience

• Strong skills in Node.js, JavaScript/TypeScript

• Experience building systems on AWS (SQS, Lambda, EC2, RDS, etc.)

• Solid understanding of distributed systems and event-driven architectures

• Experience designing and maintaining REST or GraphQL APIs

• Familiarity with SQL and NoSQL databases

• A commitment to writing unit and integration tests

• Knowledge of system design, caching, and security best practices (OWASP Top 10)

• Hands-on experience shipping production code with AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot agent mode), with clear examples of where you had to step in, correct, or override them

• Strong code review skills, applied just as rigorously to AI-generated changes

• Must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (green card holder)

Nice to have:

• AWS certification

• Experience with high-scale or business-critical systems

• Experience with pricing, quoting, or other numerically sensitive business logic

• Experience building agent workflows, custom tools, or MCP integrations for your team

How You Work

jobs.title: Director, Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
The Company
VeSync is a portfolio company with brands that cover different categories of health & wellness products. We wouldn't be surprised if you have one of our Levoit air purifiers in your living room or a COSORI air fryer whipping up healthy and delicious meals for you every night.
We're a young and energetic company, we've had tremendous success, and we are constantly growing our team. As we garner more industry attention — just check out our accomplishments and awards by CES Innovation, iF Design, IGA, and Red Dot — we also need driven and talented people to join our team.
That brings us to you, and what you'll be joining. Our teams are smart and diligent and take ownership of their work — they're confident in their work but know how to collaborate with open ears and a spirit of learning. If you're down-to-earth, approachable, and easy to strike up a conversation with, this may be a great fit for you.
Check out our other brands: levoit.com | cosori.com | etekcity.com
The Opportunity
A new ecosystem at the intersection of wellness and technology, with a connected product, hardware and software, built to help people take an active role in their own health rather than simply measure it. The Director of Growth Marketing owns how we acquire members and how we keep them.
Your job is to build the growth engine and the team behind it. You'll set the channel mix and the testing plan, carry the acquisition number and the economics under it, own the site as a growth surface, and build the lifecycle program that makes the membership work. We are pre-launch, and the brand, the positioning, and the claims we can make are all still being built. You'll start from a business case and a target rather than from an account with history. It's a leadership role, and it's a building role.
Responsibilities
Growth Strategy & Acquisition
Own the Acquisition Roadmap: Set the channel mix, the testing plan, and the sequence. Meta first, expanding across channels as we learn what works and where the audience actually is.
Own CAC and Payback: Carry the acquisition number and the economics under it. Decide what we spend, where it goes, when to push, and when to stop.
Build the Operating Model: Decide where media buying sits, agency or in house, and change it when the stage changes. Build the test and learn cadence that makes those decisions repeatable.
Team & Creative
Build the Team: Lead and grow the growth function, starting with the Creative Strategist and extending into lifecycle and media as the business supports it.
Hold the Creative Pipeline to Performance: Creative diversity is now the primary lever on the platforms. Set what gets tested, how tests are structured, and what the results mean for what gets made next.
Own Lifecycle and Retention: Build the onboarding, engagement, and renewal program that makes a membership business work, and bring in the specialist hire when the volume justifies it.
Site, Measurement & Economics
Own the Site as a Growth Surface: Own conversion, the offer, and the roadmap for what the site needs to do. Execution runs through a shared web resource, so clear specification and influence matter more than direct control.
Direct the Measurement Stack: The infrastructure will be in place, including CAPI, tag management, and the CDP. Your job is to define what it has to answer and to turn what it says into decisions.
Work the Economics: Model the relationship between CAC, payback, and lifetime value. Early cohort work is directional and shared with leadership until a dedicated analytics function is in place.
Qualifications
We are seeking a growth leader who has built an acquisition engine from zero and thinks in lifetime value rather than first-order return.
Education: Bachelor's degree required.
Experience: 8+ years in growth or performance marketing for consumer (B2C) brands, with hands-on direct-to-consumer (DTC) experience and time spent leading teams and agency partners.
Built, Not Only Scaled: Has started an acquisition program rather than inherited one. Has set a first CAC target without historical data to anchor it, and been right enough to keep going.
Thinks in Lifetime Value: Comfortable with CAC to LTV modeling, cohort behavior, and payback windows. Subscription, membership, replenishment, or any consumer business with real retention economics all count. An instinct for how value gets priced and packaged is a plus. What doesn't work here is optimizing to first-order ROAS.
Strategic and in the Details: Not the person in Ads Manager every day, but close enough to the platform to spec a test, read the result, and know when an agency is wrong.
Technically Fluent: Comfortable directing a martech and measurement stack without needing to implement it. Knows what to ask of it, and what to do with what comes back.
Comfortable with Ambiguity: Can build while the brand, the positioning, and the claims framework are still being settled. Makes progress on partial information and changes direction when decisions land.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partners closely with product marketing, brand and creative, product, ecommerce, CX, and finance.

Location: This is an on-site, office-based role in Tustin, CA.
Salary: Starting at 190K

Perks and Benefits
100% covered Medical/Dental/Vision insurance for employee AND spouse + dependents!
401K with 4% employer match (eligible after 90 days of employment) and immediate 100% vesting
Generous PTO policy + paid holidays
Life Insurance
Voluntary Life Insurance
Disability Insurance
Critical Illness Coverage
Accident Insurance
Healthcare FSA
Dependent Care FSA
Travel Assistance Program
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Fully stocked kitchen

jobs.title: Senior Event Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCKER

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________



Docker’s event portfolio - flagship conferences, developer roadshows, digital events, and community activations - is how Docker shows up in the world and turns developer enthusiasm into enterprise pipeline. As the portfolio grows, operational excellence is what lets it scale without added risk or complexity.



As a Senior Event Operations Manager, you will own the operational execution of that portfolio. Working closely with Docker's Director of Events, you coordinate planning timelines, manage vendors and logistics, own budgets and the event tech stack, and build the repeatable playbooks that keep programs running smoothly and consistently across the year.



This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building systems, bringing structure to fast-moving projects, and delivering high-quality experiences at scale. 

You will report to the Director of Events within Marketing and partner daily with Product Marketing, Developer Relations, Field Marketing, and Sales.



Please note: for this role, you must have the ability to travel 35% of the time across North America, along with international travel as-needed. 




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Success in this role is operational: events are delivered smoothly and consistently across the portfolio, teams have clear planning processes and execution frameworks to work from, and operational risks are identified early and resolved quickly. Above all, programs are able to grow and scale without increasing complexity, because the systems, playbooks, and budgets you build absorb that growth.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own operational execution across the event portfolio - major conferences, developer roadshows, digital events, and community activations - managing timelines, project plans, and execution milestones across multiple concurrent events, and keeping them on schedule, on budget, and aligned to internal goals.

 - Maintain a master event calendar that coordinates timing, resourcing, and dependencies across programs.

 - Manage event registration, attendee experience, and lead capture and badging across the portfolio.

 - Build scalable event operations: repeatable planning templates, run-of-show frameworks, and operational playbooks, continuously simplifying and improving execution over time.

 - Own the event technology stack (registration, mobile apps, lead retrieval) and ensure data flows cleanly into marketing and sales systems.

 - Manage vendors and logistics: agencies, venues, production vendors, and internal teams, including contract execution, budget tracking, shipping, production schedules, and onsite readiness.

 - Own end-to-end event budgets, including purchase orders, invoicing, and post-event reconciliation.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Product Marketing, Developer Relations, Field Marketing, and Sales, translating program goals into clear operational plans.

 - Operationalize developer-focused programs - roadshows, community activations, and flagship conference experiences - and build frameworks that let them expand to additional markets over time.

 - Track event KPIs and pipeline/ROI, run post-event debriefs, and lead reconciliation and timely handoff to sales.

 - Provide operational and logistics support to Field Marketing across regional events, roadshows, and third-party/sponsored events, including sponsorship deliverables, booth and presence logistics, and lead retrieval.




REQUIRED CANDIDATE QUALIFICATIONS

 - 6+ years in full-time, professional event management, event operations, and/or experiential program management.

 - Strong project management skills, with a track record coordinating complex programs across multiple stakeholders and concurrent events without losing attention to detail.

 - Must have the ability to travel 35% of the time across North America, with potential for international travel

 - Hands-on vendor, agency, and production-partner management, including contracts, budgets, and performance.

 - Comfortable using AI to scale repeatable processes without sacrificing quality.

 - Demonstrated professional experience with event and marketing tech (registration platforms, lead retrieval, mobile apps) and how event data flows into Salesforce and Marketo and lead management workflows.

 - Experience building operational frameworks or playbooks that let event programs scale.

 - Developer, technical, or enterprise event experience is highly preferred; background in SaaS, developer platforms, cloud, or technology companies is an advantage.

 - Comfort working in fast-moving environments where priorities can evolve.




WHAT TO EXPECT


FIRST 30 DAYS

 - Immerse in Docker’s event portfolio, the master calendar, the event tech stack, and current vendor and agency relationships.

 - Audit live programs and operational processes; identify where timelines, budgets, and handoffs carry the most risk.

 - Build working relationships with the Director of Events, Field Marketing, Product Marketing, Developer Relations, and Sales.

 - Take ownership of operational execution for the next event on the calendar.


FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Stand up or refine repeatable planning templates, run-of-show frameworks, and operational playbooks across the portfolio.

 - Establish a master event calendar that coordinates timing, resourcing, and dependencies.

 - Deliver a flagship event or roadshow end to end, on schedule and on budget, with clean lead capture and sales handoff.

 - Establish a post-event debrief and KPI/ROI reporting cadence that informs future planning and investment.


ONE-YEAR OUTLOOK

 - Run an event operations function that scales with the portfolio without adding risk or complexity.

 - Own end-to-end budgets and vendor relationships with reliable reconciliation and reporting.

 - Expand developer-focused programs to additional markets on repeatable frameworks.

 - Be the operational backbone the events and field marketing teams rely on for consistent, high-quality execution.
   
   

Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.



Compensation & Equity

United States: $102.2K – $146K + equity

______________________________________________________________________




POSTING INFORMATION

 - Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

 - AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

 - Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________




PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

 - Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

 - Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

 - Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

 - Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

 - Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

 - Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

 - Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

 - Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

 - Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.



Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community.



#LI-REMOTE

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

tl;dr: Fresh off a $15M Series A led by Accel (total funding now $20M+), Agave is experiencing hockey-stick growth. We're looking for a world-class senior full-stack/backend engineer who loves building AI and agent products on top of hard-won data, simplifying complex systems, and making them fast at scale. Learn more about us here (link).

In-person: if you're in the Bay Area, we expect you in our San Francisco office 5 days a week. The role is remote-optional for candidates outside the Bay Area, and we offer a sizable relocation bonus if you want to move here.




WHAT IS AGAVE?

We're building the financial operations platform for construction, a $12T global industry run by software built 20-40 years ago.

We have 550+ customers, backed by Accel and Y Combinator, with investors from Procore, Autodesk, and Plaid. Our three co-founders have worked together for 12+ years, across Graphiq (acquired by Amazon in 2017) and Amazon.

We've built something people actually need, in a market most of Silicon Valley ignores — which is exactly why we're winning. We've spent the last five years building the foundational data layers that give us unusually deep access to our customers' financial and project data, across systems that were never built to talk to each other. That's the moat, and you'd be joining right as we ramp up the AI-powered products that sit on top of it. The only thing slowing us down is hiring. Our team is small, scrappy, and high-caliber, and we're looking for the next wave of builders who will help take Agave from breakout startup to category-defining company.




WHY JOIN US?

Early-stage, yet de-risked: we are a rare combo of being early stage (high upside) but lower risk (thousands of contractors using us, hockey-stick growth). You get the benefits of an early stage startup without the risk you'll have at almost any other startup. You'll have a ton of impact, work directly with our customers, and get to work on interesting technical challenges you won't see at bigger companies. Although we're early stage, we've eliminated key strategic risks you'll face at other startups, like an unproven product, lack of market validation, lack of revenue, or co-founder disputes. We're all young and hungry. Most of us moved to SF from far away (Canada, SoCal, Texas, Virginia) specifically to build Agave from the ground up.

Team is technical and diverse: you'll work with a formidable founding team that's experienced, intense, and ambitious. The cofounders worked together for 10+ years, first at a startup that Amazon acquired, then at Amazon, and now at Agave. You'll learn a ton while having outsized ownership. You'll have a front-row seat to the good and bad of building a company from the ground up.

Huge opportunity without direct competition: startups are incredibly hard, so you want to join one that has a unique advantage. You don't want to spend years of your life on a company in a saturated market with tons of competition. We're seizing an opportunity that's massive (Construction is the world's third-largest industry) but also overlooked by most people in startup land. Most who can solve this problem aren't aware it exists or are too distracted by tech trends to notice. As a result, we have a multi-year head start against potential competitors, increasing our odds of success significantly. We're also backed by world-class investors (Accel, YC) and Construction insiders (Procore and Autodesk executives, founders of the largest construction tech companies like PlanGrid).

Momentum is accelerating: our AI products are the fastest-growing part of the business, with a third of new deals now including one. Channel partnerships are fueling that growth too: we signed 8 new ones in the last month alone.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Back-end/full-stack engineer with 6+ years of experience.

 - Has designed and built new large-scale systems from scratch and owned them through years of production use.

 - Deep experience with cloud infrastructure (e.g. AWS) and distributed systems in production: caching, queuing, and data consistency at scale.

 - Has debugged hard production issues end-to-end: DB performance, memory, concurrency, third-party API failures.

 - Comfortable across the full stack, and able to pick up unfamiliar or legacy systems (SQL, DLLs).

 - Has lived through scaling pain: 100x traffic growth, migrations, incident postmortems.

 - Has delivered large, ambiguous projects end-to-end, and can explain the tradeoffs to founders and customers, not just engineers.

 - Self-motivated, high ownership, low ego; desire to work on a fast-paced, intense, fun team. Excited to be our next hire; passion for building a world-class engineering culture.

 - If in Bay Area: pumped to work in-person with us in SF 5 days/week. This role is remote optional for candidates outside of the Bay Area.

 - No need to have: prior experience with our tech stack.
   
   


WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU

 - Own the architecture of major subsystems — a new integration category, sync engine internals, our AI product infrastructure. The design decisions are yours to make and defend.

 - Set the patterns the team builds on. Your abstractions become how we build; you influence through design docs, reviews, and tooling.

 - Scope and de-risk multi-week projects yourself: identify the unknowns, prototype early, sequence the work.

 - Make pragmatic build-vs-buy and tech-debt tradeoffs, and articulate the reasoning clearly.

 - Raise the team's technical bar through design reviews, pairing, and mentoring the engineers we hire alongside you.
   
   


INTERESTING TECHNICAL CHALLENGES?

AI & agents: this is where most of our new product work is. We're building agents that read, reconcile, and act on construction financial data (invoices, change orders, pay apps, budgets) inside systems that were never designed to be queried. The hard parts are grounding, getting an agent to be right about a customer's actual numbers, evaluating quality when the correct answer lives in a 30-year-old ERP, designing tools over our own APIs, and deciding what should be a deterministic pipeline versus what to leave to a model.

Unification: we unify dozens-to-hundreds of fragmented systems under a single standard that we define: data objects, data models, authentication, account-linking UX, and features like filters and pagination. It's the foundation the AI products sit on, and every new feature has to be designed generically across every system we support and plan to support.

On-prem: we're connecting with many types of on-prem systems (SQL-based, DLL-based, API-based), many built 20-40 years ago. We provide tremendous value to customers allowing them to interface with these systems in a secure, fast, reliable way, as if they're modern, cloud-based products. We need to support real-time communication and webhooks when they don't exist (e.g., using web-sockets).

Scale & speed: we're handling millions of API requests per day, and growing daily. For our products that we power with our own API (e.g. Analytics), we need to store and retrieve large amounts of data in an efficient way, building elegant caching layers to reduce latency. We ship code daily and iterate quickly based on actual feedback from paying customers (they share tons!).




TECH STACK?

TypeScript, React, Redis, Postgres, AWS - CDK, EC2




BENEFITS

 - Equity: competitive equity, so you share in the upside you're helping create.

 - Healthcare: we cover 90% of your healthcare costs with several plan options.

 - 401k: we match 100% of your contributions, up to 4% of annual salary.

 - Performance Bonuses: we offer annual performance bonuses when we hit company growth goals. For 2026, the bonus is 15% of your base salary or OTE. We've had these bonuses for the last 3 years, and expect to continue to have them in subsequent years.

 - Relocation: sizable relocation bonus for folks currently located outside of the Bay Area, and a bonus for anyone (even within the Bay Area) who moves within a 15-minute walk of our office.

 - Breakfast & Dinner, delivered: breakfast and dinner stipends through DoorDash. Plus a kitchen stocked with coffee, snacks, drinks, and more.

 - Gym: on-site gym with Peloton, squat rack, Tempo, Yoga setup, and more.

 - Visa: we sponsor Visas (H1B, TN, etc.) for candidates who are a good fit!

 - Commuter benefits: employees can make pre-tax contributions toward commuting costs, and we'll cover the full cost of a Muni pass for those using public transit.

 - Office Visits: we will provide company-sponsored trips to our HQ in SF at least every other month. We'll coordinate trips for other remote employees to coincide during "remote visit" weeks to maximize your touchpoints with teammates.




OUR OFFICE

We've built Agave in-person since day 1, and will maintain an in-person culture in San Francisco going forward for candidates in the Bay Area. We also will provide a significant relocation bonus for candidates who want to move to the Bay Area.

Our office is at 101 New Montgomery Street, San Francisco, right near Salesforce Park, coffee shops & restaurants, and a bustling downtown. We believe building in-person is a huge strategic advantage, and we hope you'll join us.




ABOUT THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

At each stage, we decide within 24hrs and update you shortly after.

Intro (15min): informal chat for you to learn more about the role. We'll ask for details on past projects. We want to know that you can code, and speak about your work clearly. You're welcome to ask lots of questions about whether working at Agave makes sense for you.

Customer Needs Problem (50min): we'll ask you to design a feature to meet a customer need based on one of our actual application components. You'll do the work to understand the requirements, translate those to specs, and iterate on the solution as you learn more about the customer's needs. This will intentionally have more ambiguity than a typical coding-style question.

Coding (50min): you'll meet with one of our SWEs. They'll ask you 1-2 coding questions in your language of preference. We'll test how you write, test, and debug solutions, and identify tradeoffs.

On-site (60min x 5, all 1:1 interviews) [In-Person in SF, we pay for the trip]: you'll interview with each co-founder and our lead dev. This will be a deeper dive into your technical abilities and overall fit. Each interview is 1hr, 45min for our questions and 15min for yours.

jobs.title: MTS - Agent Research
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary

As a research lead, you will set the research direction for this effort and spearhead the development of self-improving agents that reliably complete difficult, long-running engineering tasks. At Etched, this loop compounds: better agents help us build and optimize our systems faster, better systems expand our capacity to run more experiments, generating feedback and training data that further improve agent capabilities. Your job is to make this loop work in practice.

This requires strong research judgment. Where will better memory, context, or tooling unlock new capabilities? Which tasks benefit from structured workflows, and which require more open-ended autonomy? When do agent limitations call for changes to the harness, and when do they require custom models trained with supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning? You will set research priorities and design experiments that guide our investments in in-context learning, model training, and harness design.

You will work closely with engineers embedded across the company, with an initial focus on ASIC development, inference, and supercomputing. First, you will build the environments that let existing models do their best work through better tools, context, feedback, and in-context learning. Then, you will use the resulting trajectories and evaluations to develop specialized models where they can improve capability, reliability, or cost.

This is a hands-on research leadership role. You should be comfortable setting direction, writing and debugging code, and carrying an idea through to production. Research success means measurable improvements in the work Etched can accomplish, with disciplined use of compute.



Key Responsibilities

 - Own the research agenda for agentic systems across Etched. Identify the most important bottlenecks, prioritize promising approaches, and decide when to scale.

 - Work directly with domain engineers to understand real workflows, diagnose where agents fail, and turn those failures into research questions with concrete evaluations.

 - Develop systems for long-running tasks, including memory, context management, tool use, planning, and coordination between agents. Determine which approaches generalize across teams and which require domain-specific methods.

 - Build evaluations that measure correctness, reliability, and efficiency on real engineering tasks, and verify that gains transfer to production.

 - Train custom models using SFT, RL, and distillation, with the agent harness in the training loop. Use execution trajectories and failure analysis to guide training data and reward design.

 - Scale experiments to hundreds or thousands of concurrent agents while maintaining reproducibility, observability, and control over compute costs.



You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)

 - Strong research taste and a record of turning ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses, decisive experiments, and useful systems.

 - Excellent engineering ability. You can move between research exploration, agent experimentation, low-level debugging, and production execution, and you take responsibility for systems working reliably.

 - Experience building agents for complex, multi-step tasks, with a practical understanding of context, memory, tools, evaluation, and failure recovery.

 - Hands-on experience with LLM post-training, including SFT and RL.

 - A track record of making meaningful progress under compute and data constraints. You care about the quality of the experiment and the cost of a successful outcome.

 - High agency and comfort with unfamiliar domains. You can find the problem, acquire the missing context, and drive the work forward.

 - The ability to set technical direction and work closely with domain experts to turn research into systems they trust and use.



Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)

 - ASIC design or verification, accelerator kernels, inference systems, or large-scale compute infrastructure.



Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
   
   - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification



Base Compensation Range

 - $175K – $275K

 - Plus Significant Equity



How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.
